
FILE dist/sandbox/http-proxy.js
1: import { Agent, createServer } from 'node:http';
2: import { request as httpRequest } from 'node:http';
3: import { request as httpsRequest } from 'node:https';
4: import { connect } from 'node:net';
5: import { URL } from 'node:url';
6: import { logForDebugging } from '../utils/debug.js';
7: import { encodedCommandFromProxyUser } from './sandbox-utils.js';
8: import { CRL_PATH } from './mitm-ca.js';
9: import { decideAndRespond, rawDenied, respondDenied, respondUpstreamError, } from './request-filter.js';
10: const ALLOWLIST_DENY = [
11:     'Connection blocked by network allowlist',
12:     'blocked-by-allowlist',
13: ];
14: import { peekForClientHello, terminateAndForward, } from './tls-terminate-proxy.js';
15: import { prepareBodySubstitution, } from './body-substitution.js';
16: import { isResolvedAddressDenied } from './resolved-address-guard.js';
17: import { canonicalizeHost, connectViaParentProxy, directRequestOptions, dialDirect, formatAuthority, openConnectTunnel, proxyAuthHeader, selectParentProxyUrl, shouldBypassParentProxy, stripBrackets, stripHopByHop, } from './parent-proxy.js';
18: export function createHttpProxyServer(options) {
19:     const server = createServer();
20:     // A client that is killed mid-exchange (sandboxed process tree teardown)
21:     // resets its connection; without a listener that surfaces as an
22:     // ECONNRESET uncaughtException from node:_http_server and can take down
23:     // the host process. Parse errors get the RFC-required 400; resets and
24:     // already-unwritable sockets are just dropped.
25:     server.on('clientError', (err, socket) => {
26:         logForDebugging(`Client connection error: ${err.message}`, {
27:             level: 'error',
28:         });
29:         // The peer may reset while the 400 flushes; without a listener that
30:         // write failure is itself an uncaughtException.
31:         socket.on('error', () => { });
32:         if (err.code !== 'ECONNRESET' &&
33:             socket.writable) {
34:             // Destroy only after the flush: destroying immediately races the
35:             // write and can reset the connection before the 400 reaches the
36:             // client, while end() alone can leave a half-open socket from a
37:             // client that never closes its side. Under Bun the flush callback
38:             // may never fire on a parse-errored socket (the 400 is dropped;
39:             // verified empirically), so back-stop with a timer or the socket
40:             // leaks.
41:             const status = err.code === 'HPE_HEADER_OVERFLOW'
42:                 ? '431 Request Header Fields Too Large'
43:                 : '400 Bad Request';
44:             socket.end(`HTTP/1.1 ${status}\r\n\r\n`, () => socket.destroy());
45:             const backstop = setTimeout(() => socket.destroy(), 1000);
46:             backstop.unref?.();
47:             return;
48:         }
49:         socket.destroy();
50:     });
51:     const checkAuth = (got) => {
52:         if (!options.proxyAuthToken)
53:             return { ok: true };
54:         const m = /^basic\s+([a-z0-9+/=]+)\s*$/i.exec(got ?? '');
55:         if (!m)
56:             return { ok: false };
57:         const decoded = Buffer.from(m[1], 'base64').toString('utf8');
58:         const sep = decoded.indexOf(':');
59:         if (sep <= 0 || decoded.slice(sep + 1) !== options.proxyAuthToken) {
60:             return { ok: false };
61:         }
62:         return {
63:             ok: true,
64:             encodedCommand: encodedCommandFromProxyUser(decoded.slice(0, sep)),
65:         };
66:     };
67:     // Handle CONNECT requests for HTTPS traffic
68:     server.on('connect', async (req, socket, head) => {
69:         // Attach error handler immediately to prevent unhandled errors
70:         socket.on('error', err => {
71:             logForDebugging(`Client socket error: ${err.message}`, { level: 'error' });
72:             // A failed write (e.g. EPIPE to a dead peer) must also release
73:             // the descriptor: logging alone leaves the fd open for the life
74:             // of the process, and an open dead-peer fd is what the runtime's
75:             // EPIPE retry loop spun on (idle-CPU busy-loop incident).
76:             // destroy() is idempotent, so overlap with the close handlers
77:             // below is harmless.
78:             socket.destroy();
79:         });
80:         // Track client liveness so we can abort the upstream dial if they bail.
81:         let clientGone = false;
82:         socket.once('close', () => {
83:             clientGone = true;
84:         });
85:         // EOF during the decision window is treated as abandonment — a
86:         // half-closed client cannot run any bidirectional protocol over the
87:         // tunnel it is waiting for — so close our side immediately, the
88:         // same close every healthy cycle performs at teardown. Without
89:         // this, an EOF'd socket survives an arbitrarily long filter await
90:         // half-open (the host decision may be a model-classifier call or
91:         // an interactive permission prompt), and the verdict write lands on
92:         // a dead descriptor. The armed window runs from here through the
93:         // filter await, the ClientHello peek (MITM path), and the upstream
94:         // dial; it is disarmed only at tunnel handoff, where established
95:         // tunnels forward FIN through pipe() and keep half-open semantics —
96:         // a FIN during the dial tears the connection down rather than
97:         // half-opening it, which is the cleaner teardown for a client that
98:         // is gone.
99:         //
100:         // Deliberate tradeoff: a hypothetical pipelined send-and-FIN
101:         // CONNECT client (payload + FIN up front, then read the response
102:         // across the half-open socket) is also destroyed here. Accepting
103:         // that means nothing is written once EOF has been observed
104:         // (checked again at write time via readableEnded). EOF
105:         // notification is best-effort on a paused socket, so the layered
106:         // backstop matters: a write that still hits a dead peer errors,
107:         // and the error handler above destroys the socket, releasing the
108:         // descriptor. On runtimes whose EPIPE handling spins on dead-peer
109:         // writes (the incident's Bun builds, pre oven-sh/bun#37076) this
110:         // narrows the exposure from every abandoned decision to only those
111:         // whose EOF was never notified.
112:         const onDecisionWindowEof = () => {
113:             clientGone = true;
114:             socket.destroy();
115:         };
116:         // 'end' only fires once the stream is being read: on a paused socket
117:         // (which a CONNECT socket is, between the header parse and the tunnel
118:         // handoff) a client FIN can sit unobserved for the whole decision.
119:         // On the opaque path, capture decision-window data to put the socket
120:         // into flowing mode — making EOF notification reliable across
121:         // runtimes — and fold anything captured back into `head` at disarm
122:         // so early tunnel bytes (a client that pipelines its first payload
123:         // behind the CONNECT) are never lost.
124:         //
125:         // Deliberately NOT armed on the mitmCA path: the ClientHello peek
126:         // and the terminating relay manage this socket's flow themselves
127:         // (pull-mode reads chosen specifically because pause()/resume()
128:         // cycles corrupt CONNECT-upgraded sockets under Bun — see
129:         // relayPaused), and injecting a flowing-mode phase ahead of them
130:         // breaks the terminating path outright. There, EOF detection during
131:         // the decision stays best-effort ('close' fires on full close — the
132:         // incident case — and the peek's own reads surface 'end' once it
133:         // runs); the write-time guards and the error-handler backstop cover
134:         // the remainder.
135:         //
136:         // Capture is bounded: the paused socket used to give free TCP
137:         // backpressure, and an untrusted client streaming at line rate for
138:         // the length of an interactive permission prompt must not balloon
139:         // host memory. A legitimate pipelined first flight (an SSH banner)
140:         // is tiny; blowing the cap is abandonment-grade abuse and closes
141:         // the connection.
142:         const MAX_DECISION_CAPTURE_BYTES = 64 * 1024;
143:         let decisionCaptureBytes = 0;
144:         let capturing = false;
145:         const decisionData = [];
146:         const onDecisionData = (chunk) => {
147:             if (!capturing)
148:                 return;
149:             decisionCaptureBytes += chunk.length;
150:             if (decisionCaptureBytes > MAX_DECISION_CAPTURE_BYTES) {
151:                 logForDebugging('CONNECT client exceeded pre-establishment capture cap; destroying', { level: 'error' });
152:                 onDecisionWindowEof();
153:                 return;
154:             }
155:             decisionData.push(chunk);
156:         };
157:         if (!options.mitmCA) {
158:             capturing = true;
159:             socket.on('data', onDecisionData);
160:         }
161:         // EOF may already have been processed before this handler arms (a
162:         // client that sent CONNECT and FIN together), and an already-emitted
163:         // 'end' never re-fires — check the flag first.
164:         if (socket.readableEnded) {
165:             onDecisionWindowEof();
166:         }
167:         else {
168:             socket.once('end', onDecisionWindowEof);
169:         }
170:         // Stop capturing, folding captured bytes into `head`. The listener
171:         // deliberately STAYS attached as a discarding sink: 'data' events
172:         // broadcast to every listener, so the real consumer (pipe()) still
173:         // receives everything, while removing the last listener from a
174:         // flowing stream would silently DROP bytes arriving before the
175:         // consumer attaches (e.g. during the awaited upstream dial). No
176:         // pause() — pause/resume cycles corrupt CONNECT-upgraded sockets
177:         // under Bun (see relayPaused).
178:         const disarmDecisionCapture = () => {
179:             capturing = false;
180:             if (decisionData.length) {
181:                 head = Buffer.concat([head, ...decisionData]);
182:                 decisionData.length = 0;
183:             }
184:         };
185:         const disarmDecisionWindowEof = () => {
186:             socket.removeListener('end', onDecisionWindowEof);
187:             disarmDecisionCapture();
188:         };
189:         // Decision-phase status writes go through this guard: a verdict for
190:         // a dead client is dropped, never written. The filter's work is not
191:         // wasted — host-side allow/deny caches serve the client's retry.
192:         const endWithStatus = (payload) => {
193:             if (clientGone ||
194:                 socket.destroyed ||
195:                 socket.readableEnded ||
196:                 !socket.writable) {
197:                 logForDebugging('CONNECT client gone before status write; dropping verdict and destroying socket');
198:                 socket.destroy();
199:                 return;
200:             }
201:             // Disarm before writing: a FIN processed while this verdict is
202:             // still queued (backpressured or slow client) would otherwise
203:             // fire the armed 'end' handler and destroy() the unflushed write.
204:             disarmDecisionWindowEof();
205:             socket.end(payload);
206:         };
207:         // A client that sent CONNECT and FIN together (or closed before the
208:         // handler ran) was destroyed at arm time: return before spending a
209:         // decision — possibly an interactive permission prompt or a
210:         // classifier call — on a connection that no longer exists.
211:         if (clientGone || socket.destroyed) {
212:             return;
213:         }
214:         // Whether the MITM sniff path already wrote the 200 — hoisted so the
215:         // catch below can see it: once the 200 is out, any HTTP status line
216:         // would land inside what the client treats as tunnel payload.
217:         let wrote200 = false;
218:         try {
219:             const auth = checkAuth(req.headers['proxy-authorization']);
220:             if (!auth.ok) {
221:                 endWithStatus('HTTP/1.1 407 Proxy Authentication Required\r\n' +
222:                     'Proxy-Authenticate: Basic realm="srt"\r\n\r\n');
223:                 return;
224:             }
225:             const target = parseConnectTarget(req.url);
226:             if (!target) {
227:                 logForDebugging(`Invalid CONNECT request: ${req.url}`, {
228:                     level: 'error',
229:                 });
230:                 endWithStatus('HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request\r\n\r\n');
231:                 return;
232:             }
233:             const { hostname: requestedHost, port } = target;
234:             const allowed = await options.filter(port, requestedHost, socket, auth.encodedCommand);
235:             if (!allowed) {
236:                 logForDebugging(`Connection blocked to ${requestedHost}:${port}`, {
237:                     level: 'error',
238:                 });
239:                 endWithStatus(rawDenied(...ALLOWLIST_DENY));
240:                 return;
241:             }
242:             // The client may have died during the filter await (EOF destroy
243:             // above, or full close): there is nothing left to establish.
244:             if (clientGone || socket.destroyed) {
245:                 socket.destroy();
246:                 return;
247:             }
248:             // From here on, use the spelling the allowlist actually evaluated.
249:             // The filter canonicalizes before matching (so `Api.Example.com.`,
250:             // `127.1`, `0x7f.0.0.1` are allowed iff their canonical forms are),
251:             // and every decision below — TLS-termination exemption, MITM
252:             // routing, parent-proxy bypass, credential injection, the leaf cert
253:             // and upstream SNI, the authority we put on the wire — must key off
254:             // that same spelling. Routing off the raw one let a trailing-dot
255:             // FQDN pass the allowlist as `api.example.com`, miss every MITM
256:             // pattern, and dial out directly. Same fallback as the filter for
257:             // the (already-validated, so practically unreachable) case where
258:             // canonicalization fails, so the two layers can never disagree.
259:             const hostname = canonicalizeHost(requestedHost) ?? requestedHost;
260:             const lookup = options.lookupFor?.(port, auth.encodedCommand);
261:             // Decide upstream route:
262:             //   in-process TLS termination
263:             //   > external MITM unix socket
264:             //   > parent HTTP proxy
265:             //   > direct
266:             // (tlsTerminate and mitmProxy are mutually exclusive at the config
267:             // layer, so the first two never both apply.)
268:             if (options.mitmCA &&
269:                 (options.shouldTerminateTLS?.(hostname, port) ?? true)) {
270:                 // We can only terminate TLS. CONNECT also carries non-TLS streams —
271:                 // notably SSH on Linux, where the sandbox's own GIT_SSH_COMMAND
272:                 // routes `ssh` through this proxy via `socat - PROXY:`. Send 200 so
273:                 // the client transmits its first bytes, sniff for a ClientHello, and
274:                 // only terminate if it is one. Non-TLS falls through to the opaque
275:                 // tunnel below — i.e. base-sandbox behaviour, hostname-allowlisted
276:                 // but not content-inspected (same as the SOCKS path).
277:                 socket.write('HTTP/1.1 200 Connection Established\r\n\r\n');
278:                 wrote200 = true;
279:                 const peeked = await peekForClientHello(socket, head);
280:                 if (clientGone || socket.destroyed) {
281:                     socket.destroy();
282:                     return;
283:                 }
284:                 if (peeked.isTLS) {
285:                     disarmDecisionWindowEof();
286:                     terminateAndForward(options.mitmCA, options.filterRequest, options.mutateHeaders, options.getBodySubstitutions, socket, peeked.head, {
287:                         hostname,
288:                         port,
289:                         upstreamCA: options.tlsTerminateUpstreamCA,
290:                         lookup,
291:                         onFilterRequestDeny: options.onFilterRequestDenied
292:                             ? (method, url, reason) => options.onFilterRequestDenied({
293:                                 method,
294:                                 url,
295:                                 reason,
296:                                 encodedCommand: auth.encodedCommand,
297:                             })
298:                             : undefined,
299:                     }, options.planSigv4, options.maxSigv4ResignBodyBytes);
300:                     return;
301:                 }
302:                 logForDebugging(`[tls-terminate] non-TLS bytes on CONNECT ${hostname}:${port}; opaque-tunnelling`);
303:                 head = peeked.head;
304:             }
305:             else if (options.mitmCA) {
306:                 // Per-host termination opt-out: the policy exempts this host (mTLS
307:                 // upstream, cert-pinning client), so skip the MITM entirely and
308:                 // take the opaque tunnel below, exactly as if mitmCA were unset.
309:                 logForDebugging(`[tls-terminate] policy exempts ${hostname}:${port}; opaque-tunnelling`);
310:             }
311:             const mitmSocketPath = options.getMitmSocketPath?.(hostname);
312:             const parentUrl = !mitmSocketPath &&
313:                 options.parentProxy &&
314:                 !shouldBypassParentProxy(options.parentProxy, hostname)
315:                 ? selectParentProxyUrl(options.parentProxy, { isHttps: true })
316:                 : undefined;
317:             let upstream;
318:             try {
319:                 if (mitmSocketPath) {
320:                     logForDebugging(`Routing CONNECT ${hostname}:${port} through MITM proxy at ${mitmSocketPath}`);
321:                     upstream = await openConnectTunnel({
322:                         dial: () => connect({ path: mitmSocketPath }),
323:                         readyEvent: 'connect',
324:                         destHost: hostname,
325:                         destPort: port,
326:                     });
327:                 }
328:                 else if (parentUrl) {
329:                     upstream = await connectViaParentProxy(parentUrl, hostname, port);
330:                 }
331:                 else {
332:                     upstream = await dialDirect(hostname, port, lookup);
333:                 }
334:             }
335:             catch (err) {
336:                 logForDebugging(`CONNECT tunnel failed: ${err.message}`, {
337:                     level: 'error',
338:                 });
339:                 // If we already sent 200 (mitmCA sniff path), an HTTP status line now
340:                 // would land inside the tunnel as payload. Just close.
341:                 if (wrote200)
342:                     socket.destroy();
343:                 else if (isResolvedAddressDenied(err)) {
344:                     endWithStatus(rawDenied(err.message));
345:                 }
346:                 else
347:                     endWithStatus('HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\r\n\r\n');
348:                 return;
349:             }
350:             if (clientGone || socket.destroyed) {
351:                 upstream.on('error', () => { }); // swallow post-resolve errors
352:                 upstream.destroy();
353:                 socket.destroy();
354:                 return;
355:             }
356:             if (!wrote200) {
357:                 socket.write('HTTP/1.1 200 Connection Established\r\n\r\n');
358:             }
359:             disarmDecisionWindowEof();
360:             // An established tunnel relays each TCP direction independently: a
361:             // client that half-closes (FIN after its request bytes) must still
362:             // receive the upstream's reply. Without this, runtimes that default
363:             // http-server sockets to allowHalfOpen=false auto-close the client
364:             // side on FIN and the reply is lost.
365:             socket.allowHalfOpen = true;
366:             // Forward any bytes the client sent in the same packet as the CONNECT
367:             // (Node delivers these as the `head` buffer, not via the socket stream),
368:             // plus anything the ClientHello sniff consumed when mitmCA is on.
369:             if (head.length)
370:                 upstream.write(head);
371:             upstream.pipe(socket);
372:             socket.pipe(upstream);
373:             upstream.on('error', err => {
374:                 logForDebugging(`CONNECT tunnel failed: ${err.message}`, {
375:                     level: 'error',
376:                 });
377:                 socket.destroy();
378:             });
379:             socket.on('close', () => upstream.destroy());
380:             upstream.on('close', () => socket.destroy());
381:         }
382:         catch (err) {
383:             logForDebugging(`Error handling CONNECT: ${err}`, { level: 'error' });
384:             // Same rule as the 502 path: once the MITM sniff's 200 is out, a
385:             // status line would corrupt the tunnel byte stream — just close.
386:             if (wrote200)
387:                 socket.destroy();
388:             else
389:                 endWithStatus('HTTP/1.1 500 Internal Server Error\r\n\r\n');
390:         }
391:     });
392:     // Handle regular HTTP requests
393:     server.on('request', async (req, res) => {
394:         // A client abort mid-request destroys req/res with an error; with no
395:         // listener it escapes as an uncaughtException (the runtime emits it
396:         // from node:_http_server). `pipe()` does not forward error events, so
397:         // the body pipelines below never see it either.
398:         req.on('error', err => {
399:             logForDebugging(`Client request error: ${err.message}`, {
400:                 level: 'error',
401:             });
402:         });
403:         res.on('error', err => {
404:             logForDebugging(`Client response error: ${err.message}`, {
405:                 level: 'error',
406:             });
407:             // A failed response write (EPIPE to a dead peer) must release
408:             // the descriptor — same rationale as the CONNECT handler's
409:             // socket error handler. The res 'close' teardown listeners then
410:             // handle the upstream leg.
411:             res.socket?.destroy();
412:         });
413:         try {
414:             // Serve the empty CRL for Schannel's revocation check on MITM-minted
415:             // leaves (see MitmCA.crlDer). CryptoAPI fetches the leaf's
416:             // cRLDistributionPoints URL over plain HTTP with no
417:             // Proxy-Authorization, so this must precede both the auth check and
418:             // the `new URL(req.url)` parse below (which requires absolute-form).
419:             // Match on pathname so both origin-form (`GET /srt.crl`, what
420:             // CryptoAPI sends) and absolute-form (`GET http://…/srt.crl`, what a
421:             // proxy-aware fetcher would send) resolve; the base is ignored for
422:             // the absolute case.
423:             if (options.mitmCA &&
424:                 req.method === 'GET' &&
425:                 new URL(req.url ?? '', 'http://x').pathname === CRL_PATH) {
426:                 res.writeHead(200, {
427:                     'Content-Type': 'application/pkix-crl',
428:                     'Content-Length': options.mitmCA.crlDer.length,
429:                 });
430:                 res.end(options.mitmCA.crlDer);
431:                 return;
432:             }
433:             const auth = checkAuth(req.headers['proxy-authorization']);
434:             if (!auth.ok) {
435:                 res.writeHead(407, { 'Proxy-Authenticate': 'Basic realm="srt"' });
436:                 res.end();
437:                 return;
438:             }
439:             const url = new URL(req.url);
440:             const isHttps = url.protocol === 'https:';
441:             const defaultPort = isHttps ? 443 : 80;
442:             const requestedHost = stripBrackets(url.hostname);
443:             const port = url.port ? parseInt(url.port, 10) : defaultPort;
444:             const allowed = await options.filter(port, requestedHost, req.socket, auth.encodedCommand);
445:             if (!allowed) {
446:                 logForDebugging(`HTTP request blocked to ${requestedHost}:${port}`, {
447:                     level: 'error',
448:                 });
449:                 // The client may have aborted during the filter await; a
450:                 // deny for a dead client is dropped, not written. Plain
451:                 // half-close (EOF after a complete request) is legal HTTP
452:                 // and still gets its verdict — only a destroyed socket is
453:                 // dead here.
454:                 if (req.socket.destroyed || res.destroyed) {
455:                     res.destroy();
456:                     return;
457:                 }
458:                 respondDenied(res, ...ALLOWLIST_DENY);
459:                 return;
460:             }
461:             // Client may have disconnected while we awaited the filter; bail now
462:             // rather than dialing an upstream nobody will read from.
463:             if (req.socket.destroyed)
464:                 return;
465:             // Same rule as the CONNECT handler: everything after the allow
466:             // decision keys off the canonical spelling. The URL parser has
467:             // already lowercased and IPv4-normalized `url.hostname`; what it
468:             // leaves behind is the trailing dot, which is exactly the spelling
469:             // that used to reach getMitmSocketPath / the upstream unchanged.
470:             const hostname = canonicalizeHost(requestedHost) ?? requestedHost;
471:             // The authority we forward (request-target and Host header) is rebuilt
472:             // from the canonical host so the MITM / parent proxy sees the host we
473:             // allowlist-checked, not the client's spelling of it.
474:             const authority = formatAuthority(hostname, port, defaultPort);
475:             const fwdHeaders = { ...stripHopByHop(req.headers), host: authority };
476:             options.mutateHeadersPlaintext?.(fwdHeaders, hostname);
477:             // Body-substitution counterpart of mutateHeadersPlaintext (opt-in via
478:             // the same config gate). May delete content-length from fwdHeaders.
479:             const bodyTransform = prepareBodySubstitution(options.getBodySubstitutionsPlaintext, req, fwdHeaders, hostname);
480:             // Decide upstream route: MITM unix socket > parent HTTP proxy > direct.
481:             const mitmSocketPath = options.getMitmSocketPath?.(hostname);
482:             const parentUrl = !mitmSocketPath &&
483:                 options.parentProxy &&
484:                 !shouldBypassParentProxy(options.parentProxy, hostname)
485:                 ? selectParentProxyUrl(options.parentProxy, {
486:                     isHttps,
487:                 })
488:                 : undefined;
489:             // Reconstruct the absolute URI from parsed components rather than
490:             // forwarding the client's raw req.url. This ensures the upstream proxy
491:             // sees exactly the host we allowlist-checked, closing URL-parser
492:             // differential bypasses.
493:             const absUrl = `${url.protocol}//${authority}${url.pathname}${url.search}`;
494:             // Per-request filter applies to plain HTTP too — otherwise a sandboxed
495:             // client could bypass it by using http:// where the upstream serves it.
496:             let body = req;
497:             if (options.filterRequest) {
498:                 const ac = new AbortController();
499:                 res.once('close', () => ac.abort());
500:                 const out = await decideAndRespond(options.filterRequest, req, res, absUrl, ac.signal, options.onFilterRequestDenied
501:                     ? (method, url, reason) => options.onFilterRequestDenied({
502:                         method,
503:                         url,
504:                         reason,
505:                         encodedCommand: auth.encodedCommand,
506:                     })
507:                     : undefined);
508:                 if (out === null)
509:                     return;
510:                 body = out;
511:                 // The client may have aborted during the filterRequest await —
512:                 // the tee branch is already destroyed and res 'close' has already
513:                 // fired, so the teardown listeners attached below would never
514:                 // run. Don't dial an upstream for a dead client. A COMPLETED
515:                 // request is also destroyed=true (normal stream lifecycle after
516:                 // 'end'); only a destroy without a clean end is an abort.
517:                 if ((req.destroyed && !req.readableEnded) ||
518:                     res.destroyed ||
519:                     req.socket.destroyed ||
520:                     body.destroyed) {
521:                     body.destroy();
522:                     return;
523:                 }
524:             }
525:             // When the client declared a body but the forwarded headers carry no
526:             // framing (chunked TE stripped as hop-by-hop, or a body transform
527:             // deleted content-length), the upstream leg must re-frame
528:             // explicitly: for bodyless-method requests the runtime would
529:             // otherwise write the piped body bytes raw after complete-framed
530:             // headers — a request-smuggling primitive.
531:             const clientDeclaredBody = Boolean(req.headers['content-length'] || req.headers['transfer-encoding']);
532:             if (clientDeclaredBody &&
533:                 fwdHeaders['content-length'] === undefined &&
534:                 fwdHeaders['transfer-encoding'] === undefined) {
535:                 fwdHeaders['transfer-encoding'] = 'chunked';
536:             }
537:             const failUpstream = (err) => {
538:                 logForDebugging(`Proxy request failed: ${err.message}`, {
539:                     level: 'error',
540:                 });
541:                 respondUpstreamError(res, err);
542:             };
543:             let proxyReq;
544:             if (mitmSocketPath) {
545:                 logForDebugging(`Routing HTTP ${req.method} ${hostname}:${port} through MITM proxy at ${mitmSocketPath}`);
546:                 const mitmAgent = new Agent({
547:                     // @ts-expect-error - socketPath is valid but not in types
548:                     socketPath: mitmSocketPath,
549:                 });
550:                 proxyReq = httpRequest({
551:                     agent: mitmAgent,
552:                     path: absUrl,
553:                     method: req.method,
554:                     headers: fwdHeaders,
555:                 }, proxyRes => {
556:                     // The response stream errors independently of proxyReq (e.g.
557:                     // upstream reset mid-body after headers); pipe() does not
558:                     // handle source errors.
559:                     proxyRes.on('error', err => {
560:                         logForDebugging(`Upstream response error: ${err.message}`, {
561:                             level: 'error',
562:                         });
563:                         res.destroy();
564:                     });
565:                     res.writeHead(proxyRes.statusCode, stripHopByHop(proxyRes.headers));
566:                     proxyRes.pipe(res);
567:                 });
568:             }
569:             else if (parentUrl) {
570:                 const parentHost = stripBrackets(parentUrl.hostname);
571:                 const parentPort = Number(parentUrl.port) || (parentUrl.protocol === 'https:' ? 443 : 80);
572:                 const auth = proxyAuthHeader(parentUrl);
573:                 const requestFn = parentUrl.protocol === 'https:' ? httpsRequest : httpRequest;
574:                 proxyReq = requestFn({
575:                     hostname: parentHost,
576:                     port: parentPort,
577:                     path: absUrl,
578:                     method: req.method,
579:                     headers: auth
580:                         ? { ...fwdHeaders, 'proxy-authorization': auth }
581:                         : fwdHeaders,
582:                 }, proxyRes => {
583:                     // The response stream errors independently of proxyReq (e.g.
584:                     // upstream reset mid-body after headers); pipe() does not
585:                     // handle source errors.
586:                     proxyRes.on('error', err => {
587:                         logForDebugging(`Upstream response error: ${err.message}`, {
588:                             level: 'error',
589:                         });
590:                         res.destroy();
591:                     });
592:                     res.writeHead(proxyRes.statusCode, stripHopByHop(proxyRes.headers));
593:                     proxyRes.pipe(res);
594:                 });
595:             }
596:             else {
597:                 // Vet and pick the upstream address before any request object exists
598:                 // (see directRequestOptions); the name stays in Host and, for TLS, SNI.
599:                 let direct;
600:                 try {
601:                     direct = await directRequestOptions(hostname, port, options.lookupFor?.(port, auth.encodedCommand), isHttps);
602:                 }
603:                 catch (err) {
604:                     failUpstream(err);
605:                     return;
606:                 }
607:                 if (res.destroyed || req.socket.destroyed) {
608:                     // Client went away during the dial.
609:                     body.destroy();
610:                     return;
611:                 }
612:                 proxyReq = (isHttps ? httpsRequest : httpRequest)({
613:                     ...direct,
614:                     path: url.pathname + url.search,
615:                     method: req.method,
616:                     headers: fwdHeaders,
617:                 }, proxyRes => {
618:                     // The response stream errors independently of proxyReq (e.g.
619:                     // upstream reset mid-body after headers); pipe() does not
620:                     // handle source errors.
621:                     proxyRes.on('error', err => {
622:                         logForDebugging(`Upstream response error: ${err.message}`, {
623:                             level: 'error',
624:                         });
625:                         res.destroy();
626:                     });
627:                     res.writeHead(proxyRes.statusCode, stripHopByHop(proxyRes.headers));
628:                     proxyRes.pipe(res);
629:                 });
630:             }
631:             proxyReq.on('error', failUpstream);
632:             // Tear down the upstream request if the client goes away mid-flight.
633:             res.on('close', () => proxyReq.destroy());
634:             if (bodyTransform) {
635:                 // Errors on either side of the extra pipe stage tear the chain
636:                 // down — a stalled half-open upstream would otherwise wait for the
637:                 // client.
638:                 bodyTransform.on('error', err => proxyReq.destroy(err));
639:                 body.on('error', err => bodyTransform.destroy(err));
640:                 res.on('close', () => bodyTransform.destroy());
641:                 body.pipe(bodyTransform).pipe(proxyReq);
642:             }
643:             else {
644:                 // pipe() does not handle source errors. `body` may be a tee branch
645:                 // from decideAndRespond (not `req` itself), so a client abort
646:                 // surfaces here as an 'error' that would otherwise escape as an
647:                 // uncaughtException.
648:                 body.on('error', err => proxyReq.destroy(err));
649:                 body.pipe(proxyReq);
650:             }
651:         }
652:         catch (err) {
653:             logForDebugging(`Error handling HTTP request: ${err}`, { level: 'error' });
654:             if (!res.headersSent) {
655:                 res.writeHead(500, { 'Content-Type': 'text/plain' });
656:                 res.end('Internal Server Error');
657:             }
658:             else {
659:                 res.destroy();
660:             }
661:         }
662:     });
663:     return server;
664: }
665: /**
666:  * Parse a CONNECT request-target into host + port. Handles both plain
667:  * `host:port` and bracketed IPv6 `[::1]:port`.
668:  */
669: function parseConnectTarget(target) {
670:     const m = /^\[([^\]]+)\]:(\d+)$/.exec(target) ?? /^([^:]+):(\d+)$/.exec(target);
671:     if (!m)
672:         return undefined;
673:     const port = Number(m[2]);
674:     if (!Number.isInteger(port) || port < 1 || port > 65535)
675:         return undefined;
676:     return { hostname: m[1], port };
677: }

92: function registerCleanup() {
93:     if (cleanupRegistered) {
94:         return;
95:     }
96:     const cleanupHandler = () => reset().catch(e => {
97:         logForDebugging(`Cleanup failed in registerCleanup ${e}`, {
98:             level: 'error',
99:         });
100:     });
101:     process.once('exit', cleanupHandler);
102:     process.once('SIGINT', cleanupHandler);
103:     process.once('SIGTERM', cleanupHandler);
104:     cleanupRegistered = true;
105: }
106: /**
107:  * Attribution key to command text for every wrapped invocation, so each
108:  * producer can report (and ignoreViolations can match) the command an event
109:  * belongs to rather than the opaque key. Keys are held decoded because that
110:  * is the form the carriers deliver. Bounded FIFO: the violation store itself
111:  * only retains the last 100 events, so long-gone invocations need no entry.
112:  */
113: const MAX_COMMAND_TEXTS = 1024;
114: const commandTextsByKey = new Map();
115: /** Exported for testing. */
116: export function registerCommandText(command, options) {
117:     const key = decodeSandboxedCommand(encodeSandboxedCommand(attributionKeyFor(command, options?.commandId)));
118:     const text = options?.commandText ?? command;
119:     commandTextsByKey.delete(key);
120:     commandTextsByKey.set(key, text);
121:     while (commandTextsByKey.size > MAX_COMMAND_TEXTS) {
122:         const oldest = commandTextsByKey.keys().next().value;
123:         if (oldest === undefined)
124:             break;
125:         commandTextsByKey.delete(oldest);
126:     }
127: }
128: /**
129:  * The command text for a decoded attribution key. Keys arrive over carriers
130:  * the sandboxed process can write (the observe socket's event field, the
131:  * macOS log tag, the proxy username), so only a key this process registered
132:  * carries the embedder's own text; anything else is untrusted bytes.
133:  * Exported for testing.
134:  */
135: export function resolveCommandText(decodedKey) {
136:     return (commandTextsByKey.get(decodedKey) ??
137:         sanitizeUnregisteredCommandKey(decodedKey));
138: }
139: /**
140:  * Record a proxy-side denial in the violation store so the model sees a
141:  * structured <sandbox_violations> block alongside the raw 403 / SOCKS
142:  * failure in stderr — parity with the macOS seatbelt log monitor and the
143:  * Linux seccomp observer. The proxy is the only component that knows the
144:  * destination host of a network deny, so neither of those can produce
145:  * this line. `encodedCommand` (from the proxy username) attributes it to
146:  * the invocation; without one the event is stored unattributed.
147:  */
148: function recordProxyViolation(line, encodedCommand) {
149:     const command = encodedCommand
150:         ? resolveCommandText(decodeSandboxedCommand(encodedCommand))
151:         : undefined;
152:     // Same suppression the seatbelt / seccomp monitors apply, so a
153:     // configured ignoreViolations pattern silences the event no matter
154:     // which producer saw it.
155:     if (shouldIgnoreViolation(line, command, config?.ignoreViolations)) {
156:         return;
157:     }
158:     sandboxViolationStore.addViolation({
159:         line,
160:         encodedCommand,
161:         command,
162:         timestamp: new Date(),
163:     });
164: }
165: function recordOutboundDeny(host, port, reason, encodedCommand) {
166:     recordProxyViolation(`deny network-outbound ${host}:${port} (${reason})`, encodedCommand);
167: }
168: /** Direct-dial `lookup` for the proxies: the current guard's, with a refusal recorded as a violation. */
169: const directLookup = (port, encodedCommand) => (hostname, options, callback) => resolvedAddressGuard.lookupFor(port)(hostname, options, (err, address, family) => {
170:     if (isResolvedAddressDenied(err)) {
171:         recordOutboundDeny(hostname, port, err.reason, encodedCommand);
172:     }
173:     callback(err, address, family);
174: });
175: /**
176:  * The request URL as it should appear in a model-visible violation line:
177:  * origin + path, with any query string reduced to a `?…` marker (origin
178:  * carries no userinfo, so an embedded `name:pass@` is dropped too). Query
179:  * strings routinely carry credentials (api_key=, access_token=, signed
180:  * URLs) that the sandboxed client interpolated at runtime and that were
181:  * never in the model's context, so they must not enter the transcript via
182:  * the <sandbox_violations> block. The full URL still reaches the embedder's
183:  * filterRequest callback and its own debug logging.
184:  */
185: function redactUrlForViolation(url) {
186:     try {
187:         const u = new URL(url);
188:         return `${u.origin}${u.pathname}${u.search ? '?…' : ''}`;
189:     }
190:     catch {
191:         // Not an absolute URL (shouldn't happen for proxy requests) — drop
192:         // anything after '?' rather than risk leaking it.
193:         const q = url.indexOf('?');
194:         return q === -1 ? url : `${url.slice(0, q)}?…`;
195:     }
196: }
197: async function filterNetworkRequest(port, host, sandboxAskCallback, encodedCommand) {
198:     const denied = (reason) => {
199:         recordOutboundDeny(host, port, reason, encodedCommand);
200:         return false;
201:     };
202:     if (!config) {
203:         logForDebugging('No config available, denying network request');
204:         return denied('sandbox policy unavailable');
205:     }
206:     // Reject hosts containing control characters before pattern matching.
207:     // `matchesDomainPattern` uses string suffix matching which is trivially
208:     // fooled by e.g. `evil.com\x00.allowed.com` — the null byte passes
209:     // `.endsWith()` but truncates at the libc DNS layer. The SOCKS path is the
210:     // main exposure (DOMAINNAME is unvalidated bytes); HTTP is protected by
211:     // llhttp/URL parsing, but we check here for defence in depth.
212:     if (!isValidHost(host)) {
213:         logForDebugging(`Denying malformed host: ${JSON.stringify(host)}:${port}`, {
214:             level: 'error',
215:         });
216:         return denied('malformed host');
217:     }
218:     // Canonicalize so string comparisons match what getaddrinfo() will dial.
219:     // Without this, inet_aton shorthand like `2852039166` (= 169.254.169.254)
220:     // or `127.1` slips past a denylist entry for the dotted-decimal form.
221:     const canonicalHost = canonicalizeHost(host) ?? host;
222:     // Check denied domains first
223:     for (const deniedDomain of config.network.deniedDomains) {
224:         if (matchesDomainPatternWithPort(canonicalHost, port, deniedDomain)) {
225:             logForDebugging(`Denied by config rule: ${host}:${port}`);
226:             // The matched entry's own reason when the caller supplied one, so the
227:             // model reads why this destination is off-limits (and the sanctioned
228:             // alternative) instead of a generic deny; keyed by the exact entry.
229:             return denied(config.network.deniedDomainReasons?.[deniedDomain] ??
230:                 'host is on the deny list');
231:         }
232:     }
233:     // Check allowed domains
234:     for (const allowedDomain of config.network.allowedDomains) {
235:         if (matchesDomainPatternWithPort(canonicalHost, port, allowedDomain)) {
236:             logForDebugging(`Allowed by config rule: ${host}:${port}`);
237:             return true;
238:         }
239:     }
240:     // No matching rules - ask user or deny. strictAllowlist makes the
241:     // allowlist deterministic enforcement: never fall through to the callback.
242:     if (!sandboxAskCallback || config.network.strictAllowlist) {
243:         logForDebugging(`No matching config rule, denying: ${host}:${port}`);
244:         return denied('host is not on the allow list');
245:     }
246:     logForDebugging(`No matching config rule, asking user: ${host}:${port}`);
247:     try {
248:         const userAllowed = await sandboxAskCallback({ host, port });
249:         if (userAllowed) {
250:             logForDebugging(`User allowed: ${host}:${port}`);
251:             return true;
252:         }
253:         logForDebugging(`User denied: ${host}:${port}`);
254:         return denied('user denied');
255:     }
256:     catch (error) {
257:         logForDebugging(`Error in permission callback: ${error}`, {
258:             level: 'error',
259:         });
260:         return denied('permission prompt failed');
261:     }
262: }
263: /**
264:  * Build the header-mutation callback that substitutes sentinel→real for
265:  * masked credentials. Returns undefined when no `credentials` block is
266:  * configured — wiring the seam at all is unnecessary then.
267:  *
268:  * Per-host gating happens inside the registry: each sentinel carries its
269:  * own injectHosts list and substitutes independently, so credential A's
270:  * sentinel cannot be laundered through credential B's allowed host. The
271:  * returned closure does not log header values; the registry holds the only
272:  * copy of the real value.
273:  */
274: function buildCredentialInjector() {
275:     if (!config?.credentials)
276:         return undefined;
277:     return (headers, destHost) => {
278:         sentinelRegistry.substituteInHeaders(headers, destHost, matchesDomainPattern);
279:     };
280: }
281: /**
282:  * Body counterpart of {@link buildCredentialInjector}: per-destination
283:  * sentinel→real pairs for streaming substitution in request bodies, with
284:  * the same per-credential injectHosts gating applied inside the registry.
285:  */
286: function buildBodyCredentialInjector() {
287:     if (!config?.credentials)
288:         return undefined;
289:     return destHost => sentinelRegistry.sentinelsForHost(destHost, matchesDomainPattern);
290: }
291: /**
292:  * Build the per-request SigV4 hook for the TLS-terminating proxy.
293:  * Returns undefined when no `credentials` block is configured. The hook
294:  * consults {@link awsPairRegistry} at request time, so pairs registered
295:  * later (wrapWithSandbox runs after the proxy starts) are picked up.
296:  */
297: function buildSigv4Planner() {
298:     if (!config?.credentials)
299:         return undefined;
300:     // Re-read the policies per request (not captured at proxy start) so an
301:     // updateConfig() that changes credentials.sigv4 takes effect without a
302:     // proxy restart, matching how the injector sees live registry state.
303:     return (method, requestTarget, headers, destHost) => createSigv4Planner(awsPairRegistry, config?.credentials?.sigv4, matchesDomainPattern)(method, requestTarget, headers, destHost);
304: }
305: /**
306:  * Get the MITM proxy socket path for a given host, if configured.
307:  * Returns the socket path if the host matches any MITM domain pattern,
308:  * otherwise returns undefined.
309:  *
310:  * Matches the canonicalized hostname, like the allow/deny filter
311:  * (filterNetworkRequest) and the tlsTerminate exclusion below. This site
312:  * fails OPEN on a miss — a host that matches no MITM pattern is dialed
313:  * directly — so it must accept exactly the set of spellings the allowlist
314:  * accepts: otherwise `api.example.com.` (trailing-dot FQDN, same name to
315:  * DNS) passes the allowlist as `api.example.com` but misses every MITM
316:  * pattern and skips the MITM proxy entirely. The proxies already hand this
317:  * hook the canonical spelling; canonicalizing again here is defence in
318:  * depth for any other caller.
319:  */
320: function getMitmSocketPath(host) {
321:     if (!config?.network.mitmProxy) {
322:         return undefined;
323:     }
324:     const { socketPath, domains } = config.network.mitmProxy;
325:     const canonicalHost = canonicalizeHost(host) ?? host;
326:     for (const pattern of domains) {
327:         if (matchesDomainPattern(canonicalHost, pattern)) {
328:             logForDebugging(`Host ${host} matches MITM pattern ${pattern}`);
329:             return socketPath;
330:         }
331:     }
332:     return undefined;
333: }
334: /**
335:  * Per-host TLS-termination opt-out from network.tlsTerminate.excludeDomains.
336:  * Only consulted by the HTTP proxy when tlsTerminate is enabled; exempted
337:  * hosts fall back to the opaque CONNECT tunnel (still allowlist-filtered),
338:  * so mTLS / cert-pinning clients can complete their own handshake.
339:  *
340:  * Matches the canonicalized hostname, like the allow/deny filter
341:  * (filterNetworkRequest) — otherwise a spelling the allowlist accepts after
342:  * canonicalization (`127.1`, a trailing-dot FQDN) would dodge the exclusion
343:  * and get terminated anyway.
344:  */
345: function shouldTerminateTLSForHost(host) {
346:     const excludeDomains = config?.network.tlsTerminate?.excludeDomains;
347:     if (!excludeDomains?.length)
348:         return true;
349:     const canonicalHost = canonicalizeHost(host) ?? host;
350:     for (const pattern of excludeDomains) {
351:         if (!matchesDomainPattern(canonicalHost, pattern))
352:             continue;
353:         logForDebugging(`Host ${host} matches tlsTerminate.excludeDomains pattern ${pattern}; skipping TLS termination`);
354:         // Masked-credential substitution only happens on the terminated path,
355:         // so a credential whose injectHosts cover this host can never be
356:         // injected here — the upstream gets the placeholder. Config validation
357:         // rejects the fully-contradictory spellings; this flags the partial
358:         // ones (e.g. default injectHosts = allowedDomains) at the moment they
359:         // actually bite.
360:         const masked = sentinelRegistry.namesInjectableAt(canonicalHost, matchesDomainPattern);
361:         if (masked.length > 0) {
362:             logForDebugging(`tlsTerminate.excludeDomains: masked credential(s) ${masked.join(', ')} ` +
363:                 `are configured for injection at ${host}, but its connections are ` +
364:                 `not terminated, so the upstream will receive the placeholder`, { level: 'error' });
365:         }
366:         return false;
367:     }
368:     return true;
369: }
370: async function startMuxProxyServer(sandboxAskCallback, portRange) {
371:     const injectCredentials = buildCredentialInjector();
372:     const injectBodyCredentials = buildBodyCredentialInjector();
373:     httpProxyServer = createHttpProxyServer({
374:         filter: (port, host, _socket, encodedCommand) => filterNetworkRequest(port, host, sandboxAskCallback, encodedCommand),
375:         getMitmSocketPath,
376:         mitmCA,
377:         shouldTerminateTLS: shouldTerminateTLSForHost,
378:         filterRequest: config?.network.filterRequest,
379:         onFilterRequestDenied: ({ method, url, reason, encodedCommand }) => {
380:             recordProxyViolation(`deny http-request ${method} ${redactUrlForViolation(url)} (${reason})`, encodedCommand);
381:         },
382:         // TLS-terminated path always gets the injector; the plain-HTTP path
383:         // only when explicitly opted in. Without the opt-in, a sentinel sent
384:         // over plain HTTP reaches the upstream unchanged (fails closed).
385:         mutateHeaders: injectCredentials,
386:         mutateHeadersPlaintext: config?.credentials?.allowPlaintextInject
387:             ? injectCredentials
388:             : undefined,
389:         getBodySubstitutions: injectBodyCredentials,
390:         getBodySubstitutionsPlaintext: config?.credentials?.allowPlaintextInject
391:             ? injectBodyCredentials
392:             : undefined,
393:         // SigV4 re-signing is TLS-terminated-path only, like credential
394:         // injection: the real signature must not travel over plaintext.
395:         planSigv4: buildSigv4Planner(),
396:         parentProxy,
397:         lookupFor: directLookup,
398:         proxyAuthToken,
399:     });
400:     socksProxyServer = createSocksProxyServer({
401:         filter: (port, host, encodedCommand) => filterNetworkRequest(port, host, sandboxAskCallback, encodedCommand),
402:         parentProxy,
403:         lookupFor: directLookup,
404:         proxyAuthToken,
405:         probeUnauthenticated: async (port, host) => {
406:             // Explicit deny rules only: an unauthenticated peer must never reach
407:             // the ask callback, and a merely off-list host gets the generic
408:             // cannot-authenticate refusal rather than a policy claim.
409:             if (!config)
410:                 return {};
411:             const canonical = canonicalizeHost(host) ?? host;
412:             for (const entry of config.network.deniedDomains) {
413:                 if (matchesDomainPatternWithPort(canonical, port, entry)) {
414:                     const reason = config.network.deniedDomainReasons?.[entry] ??
415:                         'host is on the deny list';
416:                     recordOutboundDeny(host, port, reason);
417:                     return { deniedReason: reason };
418:                 }
419:             }
420:             return {};
421:         },
422:     });
423:     muxProxyServer = createMuxProxyServer({
424:         httpServer: httpProxyServer,
425:         handleSocksConnection: s => socksProxyServer.handleConnection(s),
426:         httpBackendPortRange: portRange,
427:     });
428:     const mux = muxProxyServer;
429:     // Backend first so the front-end never accepts a connection that would
430:     // dispatch to an unbound backend. On Windows the backend's port is
431:     // excluded when binding the front-end in the same WFP range.
432:     const backendPort = await mux.listenHttpBackend();
433:     await listenInRange(mux.server, p => mux.server.listen(p, '127.0.0.1'), portRange, backendPort !== undefined ? new Set([backendPort]) : new Set());
434:     const muxPort = mux.getPort();
435:     if (muxPort === undefined) {
436:         throw new Error('Failed to get mux proxy server port');
437:     }
438:     mux.unref();
439:     logForDebugging(`Mux proxy (HTTP+SOCKS) listening on localhost:${muxPort}`);
440:     return muxPort;
441: }
442: // ============================================================================
443: // Public Module Functions (will be exported via namespace)
444: // ============================================================================
445: async function initialize(runtimeConfig, sandboxAskCallback, enableLogMonitor = false) {
446:     // Return if already initializing
447:     if (initializationPromise) {
448:         await initializationPromise;
449:         return;
450:     }
451:     // Store config for use by other functions
452:     config = runtimeConfig;
453:     // Resolve parent/upstream proxy from config or HTTP_PROXY env before we
454:     // start our own listeners (which will later shadow those vars in the child).
455:     parentProxy = resolveParentProxy(runtimeConfig.network.parentProxy);
456:     if (parentProxy) {
457:         logForDebugging(`Parent proxy configured: http=${redactUrl(parentProxy.httpUrl)} ` +
458:             `https=${redactUrl(parentProxy.httpsUrl)}`);
459:     }
460:     resolvedAddressGuard = createResolvedAddressGuard(runtimeConfig.network);
461:     // Load TLS-termination CA if configured. Throws on unreadable/non-PEM —
462:     // tlsTerminate is explicit opt-in, so a bad config is a hard error.
463:     if (runtimeConfig.network.tlsTerminate && runtimeConfig.network.mitmProxy) {
464:         throw new Error('network.tlsTerminate and network.mitmProxy are mutually exclusive');
465:     }
466:     // On Windows with tlsTerminate and no explicit caCertPath/caKeyPath,
467:     // defer CA creation until the Windows block below has resolved
468:     // srt-win and fetched user status — the persistent CA is
469:     // generated-if-absent under windowsStateDir()/ca and
470:     // trusted in the sandbox user's Root store, then loaded here.
471:     // Explicit paths (or non-Windows) go straight to createMitmCA.
472:     const tlsTerminate = runtimeConfig.network.tlsTerminate;
473:     const useWindowsPersistentCa = getPlatform() === 'windows' &&
474:         tlsTerminate !== undefined &&
475:         !tlsTerminate.caCertPath &&
476:         !tlsTerminate.caKeyPath;
477:     mitmCA =
478:         tlsTerminate && !useWindowsPersistentCa
479:             ? createMitmCA(tlsTerminate)
480:             : undefined;
481:     // Check dependencies
482:     const deps = await checkDependenciesAsync();
483:     if (deps.errors.length > 0) {
484:         throw new Error(`Sandbox dependencies not available: ${deps.errors.join(', ')}`);
485:     }
486:     // Start log monitor for macOS if enabled
487:     if (enableLogMonitor && getPlatform() === 'macos') {
488:         logMonitorShutdown = startMacOSSandboxLogMonitor(sandboxViolationStore.addViolation.bind(sandboxViolationStore), config.ignoreViolations, resolveCommandText);
489:         logForDebugging('Started macOS sandbox log monitor');
490:     }
491:     if (enableLogMonitor && getPlatform() === 'linux') {
492:         // The monitor compares paths the kernel reported, so its lists are
493:         // expanded the way the wrapper expands them (getFsWriteConfig folds in
494:         // the default write paths and drops the globs bwrap cannot take;
495:         // normalizePathForSandbox resolves `~`, relative spellings and symlinks),
496:         // plus the built-in write denies the wrapper always applies.
497:         // It does not reproduce the wrapper's existence and boundary-symlink
498:         // filters, nor the ripgrep scan for nested dangerous paths; and it still
499:         // reports writes bwrap permits through `--dev`, `--proc` and the tmpfs
500:         // over each read-denied directory. Started once, so both lists are fixed
501:         // at the cwd and configuration of this call.
502:         const monitoredWrites = getFsWriteConfig();
503:         linuxMonitor = startLinuxSandboxViolationMonitor(sandboxViolationStore.addViolation.bind(sandboxViolationStore), {
504:             // apply-seccomp's observer reports every write-intent syscall
505:             // (allowed or not). Only paths bwrap would actually refuse — outside
506:             // allowWrite or inside a denyWrite carve-out — go to the store. With
507:             // the policy on, the default write paths are listed in full rather
508:             // than as getFsWriteConfig() narrowed them: a home directory it leaves
509:             // out because it is read-denied sits under that deny's writable
510:             // tmpfs, so a write there is permitted and is not a violation.
511:             allowWritePaths: [
512:                 ...monitoredWrites.allowOnly,
513:                 ...(config.filesystem.disabled ? [] : getDefaultWritePaths()),
514:             ].map(p => normalizePathForSandbox(p)),
515:             denyWritePaths: [
516:                 ...monitoredWrites.denyWithinAllow.map(p => normalizePathForSandbox(p)),
517:                 // filesystem.disabled reaches the wrapper as `writeConfig ===
518:                 // undefined`, which skips every bind and the built-in denies with
519:                 // them, so the monitor must not judge by them either.
520:                 ...(config.filesystem.disabled
521:                     ? []
522:                     : linuxGetCwdMandatoryDenyPaths(getAllowGitConfig())),
523:             ],
524:             ignoreViolations: config.ignoreViolations,
525:             resolveCommandText,
526:         });
527:         // Don't block initialization on listen() — wrap-time checks
528:         // fs.existsSync(observeSocketPath) and degrades gracefully.
529:         void linuxMonitor.ready;
530:         logForDebugging('Started Linux seccomp violation monitor');
531:     }
532:     // Register cleanup handlers first time
533:     registerCleanup();
534:     // Windows: validate provisioning + filesystem config BEFORE any
535:     // sandboxed child can be spawned. Doing this at initialize() (not
536:     // wrap-time) means the host gets a single actionable error before
537:     // any per-exec work happens, instead of exit-15 on every command.
538:     if (getPlatform() === 'windows') {
539:         // Resolve once (stats disk); captured module-level for wrap/reset.
540:         srtWinSpawn = resolveSrtWin(runtimeConfig.windows?.srtWin);
541:         const srtWin = srtWinSpawn;
542:         const u = await getWindowsSandboxUserStatusAsync({ srtWin });
543:         if (!u.provisioned || !u.credPresent) {
544:             config = undefined;
545:             throw new WindowsSandboxError('not_provisioned', `Windows sandbox user is not provisioned (user=` +
546:                 `${u.provisioned}, cred=${u.credPresent}). Run \`npx ` +
547:                 `sandbox-runtime windows-install\` (one UAC prompt) to ` +
548:                 `provision it.`);
549:         }
550:         // Behavioral proof the WFP egress fence is active for the
551:         // sandbox user — BFE enumeration (`wfp status`) is admin-gated,
552:         // so this is the non-elevated readiness check. Fails closed: a
553:         // stale install (user provisioned but filters since removed)
554:         // throws here instead of running every exec with full egress.
555:         // After the user-status check so the not-provisioned message is
556:         // the actionable one. Once per process — the fence is install-
557:         // scoped, not session-scoped.
558:         if (!windowsWfpVerified) {
559:             try {
560:                 await verifyWindowsWfpEgress({
561:                     proxyPortRange: runtimeConfig.windows?.proxyPortRange,
562:                     srtWin,
563:                 });
564:             }
565:             catch (e) {
566:                 config = undefined;
567:                 throw e;
568:             }
569:             windowsWfpVerified = true;
570:         }
571:         // Persistent-CA branch (see the deferral comment above).
572:         // `ensurePersistentWindowsCa` reconciles the registry thumb
573:         // itself (so initialize() after uninstall→reinstall repairs
574:         // trust) and may make `u.caCertThumb` stale — hence the
575:         // explicit-path thumb check below skips this branch.
576:         if (useWindowsPersistentCa && tlsTerminate) {
577:             try {
578:                 const p = await ensurePersistentWindowsCa({ status: u, srtWin });
579:                 mitmCA = createMitmCA({
580:                     caCertPem: p.certPem,
581:                     caKeyPem: p.keyPem,
582:                     caCertPath: p.certPath,
583:                     caKeyPath: p.keyPath,
584:                     extraCaCertPaths: tlsTerminate.extraCaCertPaths,
585:                 });
586:             }
587:             catch (e) {
588:                 config = undefined;
589:                 throw e;
590:             }
591:         }
592:         // Explicit-path branch: schannel clients (System32 curl, IWR,
593:         // .NET, default-backend git) only trust what's in the sandbox
594:         // user's `CurrentUser\Root` — which `srt-win exec` does not (and
595:         // must not) write. Compare thumbprints so a stale install-time
596:         // CA doesn't pass the gate while schannel rejects the session's
597:         // proxy-minted leaves.
598:         if (tlsTerminate && mitmCA && !useWindowsPersistentCa) {
599:             const installed = getWindowsSandboxCaCert(u);
600:             const sessionThumb = certThumbprint(mitmCA.certPem);
601:             if (!installed) {
602:                 config = undefined;
603:                 throw new WindowsSandboxError('trust_ca_not_installed', `tlsTerminate on Windows requires the sandbox to be ` +
604:                     `installed with this CA (thumb=${sessionThumb}): run ` +
605:                     `\`srt-win user trust-ca ${mitmCA.certPath}\`. Per-exec ` +
606:                     `installs into the sandbox user's Root store are not ` +
607:                     `supported.`);
608:             }
609:             if (installed.thumb !== sessionThumb) {
610:                 config = undefined;
611:                 throw new WindowsSandboxError('trust_ca_thumbprint_mismatch', `tlsTerminate on Windows: the sandbox's installed CA ` +
612:                     `(thumb=${installed.thumb}) doesn't match this ` +
613:                     `session's CA (thumb=${sessionThumb}). Run \`srt-win ` +
614:                     `user trust-ca ${mitmCA.certPath}\` to update it.`);
615:             }
616:         }
617:         // Filesystem grants/denies — additive sandbox-user ACEs.
618:         try {
619:             const acc = computeWindowsFsAccessSet(runtimeConfig);
620:             // The trust bundle the CA-trust env vars point at
621:             // (NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS etc.) must be readable by the
622:             // srt-sandbox child. It's written into the broker's %TEMP%,
623:             // which the sandbox user has no inherent rights on, so it
624:             // rides the same session-level `acl grant` read-set as the
625:             // working tree. Granted on the mkdtemp DIR (not the file)
626:             // so the (OI)(CI) ACE covers both the file open AND the
627:             // parent-directory list that cmd's `type`/`FindFirstFile`
628:             // does before opening. Mirrors the mac/linux
629:             // `expandedAllowRead` push in wrapWithSandbox.
630:             if (mitmCA) {
631:                 acc.grantRead.push(dirname(mitmCA.trustBundlePath));
632:             }
633:             // `u` was fetched once above for the provisioning gate; the
634:             // same status carries the SID — don't re-spawn `srt-win user
635:             // status` here.
636:             if (!u.sid) {
637:                 throw new Error('sandbox user SID missing from `srt-win user status` ' +
638:                     '(provisioned but in an inconsistent state)');
639:             }
640:             const sb = u.sid;
641:             // Record module-level state BEFORE the first acl call so the
642:             // catch's best-effort revoke/restore can address whatever
643:             // partially landed.
644:             windowsFsSbUserSid = sb;
645:             // Grant FIRST so the sandbox user has working-tree access by
646:             // the time the deny stamp runs. The two are independent
647:             // refcounted state-DB sets keyed on the same holder PID.
648:             if (acc.grantRead.length > 0 || acc.grantWrite.length > 0) {
649:                 grantWindowsAcl({
650:                     sandboxUserSid: sb,
651:                     read: acc.grantRead,
652:                     write: acc.grantWrite,
653:                     srtWin,
654:                 });
655:             }
656:             if (acc.denyRead.length > 0 || acc.denyWrite.length > 0) {
657:                 stampWindowsAcl({
658:                     sandboxUserSid: sb,
659:                     denyRead: acc.denyRead,
660:                     denyWrite: acc.denyWrite,
661:                     srtWin,
662:                 });
663:             }
664:             // Only record when something was actually applied — gates
665:             // running revoke/restore at reset(). Recorded AFTER success —
666:             // the catch below clears `config`, and a non-undefined
667:             // stampedSet would leave reset()/updateConfig() seeing state
668:             // that never landed.
669:             const anyApplied = acc.grantRead.length > 0 ||
670:                 acc.grantWrite.length > 0 ||
671:                 acc.denyRead.length > 0 ||
672:                 acc.denyWrite.length > 0;
673:             if (anyApplied) {
674:                 windowsFsStampedSet = acc;
675:                 logForDebugging(`[Sandbox Windows] fs applied: ` +
676:                     `${acc.grantWrite.length} grantWrite, ` +
677:                     `${acc.grantRead.length} grantRead, ` +
678:                     `${acc.denyRead.length} denyRead, ` +
679:                     `${acc.denyWrite.length} denyWrite`);
680:             }
681:             windowsFsRawInputs = rawWindowsFsInputs(runtimeConfig);
682:         }
683:         catch (e) {
684:             // Best-effort release of whatever WAS applied before the
685:             // failure (exit-2 partial stamps/grants the resolvable
686:             // inputs; harmless if nothing was — no holds for this PID).
687:             if (windowsFsSbUserSid) {
688:                 revokeWindowsAcl({ sandboxUserSid: windowsFsSbUserSid, srtWin });
689:                 restoreWindowsAcl({ sandboxUserSid: windowsFsSbUserSid, srtWin });
690:             }
691:             windowsFsSbUserSid = undefined;
692:             config = undefined;
693:             throw e;
694:         }
695:     }
696:     // Initialize network infrastructure
697:     initializationPromise = (async () => {
698:         try {
699:             // On Windows the WFP loopback permit covers a fixed port
700:             // range, so the proxies must bind inside it. Other platforms
701:             // bake the actual ephemeral port into the sandbox profile, so
702:             // they keep using port 0.
703:             const portRange = getPlatform() === 'windows'
704:                 ? (config.windows?.proxyPortRange ?? DEFAULT_WINDOWS_PROXY_PORT_RANGE)
705:                 : undefined;
706:             // The auth token is only set when this process owns the proxy; an
707:             // external proxy (config.network.httpProxyPort) handles its own auth,
708:             // and embedding our token in its URL would be wrong.
709:             proxyAuthToken =
710:                 config.network.httpProxyPort !== undefined
711:                     ? undefined
712:                     : randomBytes(16).toString('hex');
713:             // The mux front-end serves both protocols on one port. Each side's
714:             // reported port is the external override if configured, else the mux
715:             // port — so the public config.network.{http,socks}ProxyPort contract
716:             // is unchanged. The mux is skipped only when BOTH are external.
717:             const needLocalProxy = config.network.httpProxyPort === undefined ||
718:                 config.network.socksProxyPort === undefined;
719:             const muxPort = needLocalProxy
720:                 ? await startMuxProxyServer(sandboxAskCallback, portRange)
721:                 : undefined;
722:             const httpProxyPort = config.network.httpProxyPort ?? muxPort;
723:             const socksProxyPort = config.network.socksProxyPort ?? muxPort;
724:             // JVMs read neither HTTPS_PROXY nor its credential; the agent bridges
725:             // both. Resolved once here, advertised via JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS per command.
726:             // Async: the global-npm fallback spawns `npm root -g`.
727:             javaAgentJarPath =
728:                 (await getJavaProxyAgentJarPathAsync(config.javaAgentJarPath)) ??
729:                     undefined;
730:             // Leaves are minted lazily per-CONNECT (after this point), so setting
731:             // the CDP URL now means every leaf carries it. See MitmCA.crlUrl.
732:             // Windows-only: on Linux the child runs under bwrap --unshare-net and
733:             // reaches the proxy via a socat bridge on a fixed netns port, so a
734:             // host-namespace mux port would be unreachable — worse than no CDP,
735:             // since a Schannel-analog client (Java, OpenSSL with CRL_CHECK) then
736:             // hard-fails "CRL fetch error" instead of soft-passing "no CDP". macOS
737:             // has no in-tree Schannel-analog client. Also gated on `muxPort`: an
738:             // external `network.httpProxyPort` doesn't answer /srt.crl.
739:             if (mitmCA && muxPort !== undefined && getPlatform() === 'windows') {
740:                 mitmCA.crlUrl = `http://127.0.0.1:${muxPort}${CRL_PATH}`;
741:             }
742:             if (config.network.httpProxyPort !== undefined) {
743:                 logForDebugging(`Using external HTTP proxy on port ${httpProxyPort}`);
744:             }
745:             if (config.network.socksProxyPort !== undefined) {
746:                 logForDebugging(`Using external SOCKS proxy on port ${socksProxyPort}`);
747:             }
748:             // Initialize platform-specific infrastructure
749:             let linuxBridge;
750:             if (getPlatform() === 'linux') {
751:                 linuxBridge = await initializeLinuxNetworkBridge(httpProxyPort, socksProxyPort, config.socatPath);
752:             }
753:             const context = {
754:                 httpProxyPort,
755:                 socksProxyPort,
756:                 linuxBridge,
757:             };
758:             managerContext = context;
759:             logForDebugging('Network infrastructure initialized');
760:             return context;
761:         }
762:         catch (error) {
763:             // Clear state on error so initialization can be retried
764:             initializationPromise = undefined;
765:             managerContext = undefined;
766:             reset().catch(e => {
767:                 logForDebugging(`Cleanup failed in initializationPromise ${e}`, {
768:                     level: 'error',
769:                 });
770:             });
771:             throw error;
772:         }
773:     })();
774:     await initializationPromise;
775: }
776: function isSupportedPlatform() {
777:     const platform = getPlatform();
778:     if (platform === 'linux') {
779:         // WSL1 doesn't support bubblewrap
780:         return getWslVersion() !== '1';
781:     }
782:     return platform === 'macos' || platform === 'windows';
783: }
784: function isSandboxingEnabled() {
785:     // Sandboxing is enabled if config has been set (via initialize())
786:     return config !== undefined;
787: }
788: /**
789:  * Platform-independent part of the dependency check. Returns either
790:  * a finished result (POSIX, unsupported platform, or a Windows
791:  * srt-win resolution failure) or the inputs for the Windows probe —
792:  * the only platform where the sync and async variants differ.
793:  */
794: function checkDependenciesCommon(ripgrepConfig) {
795:     if (!isSupportedPlatform()) {
796:         return { done: { errors: ['Unsupported platform'], warnings: [] } };
797:     }
798:     const errors = [];
799:     const warnings = [];
800:     const platform = getPlatform();
801:     if (platform === 'linux') {
802:         // ripgrep is Linux-only: it's used by linuxGetMandatoryDenyPaths() to
803:         // expand glob deny-patterns to concrete paths for bwrap. macOS seatbelt
804:         // profiles take regex patterns directly, so rg is never invoked there.
805:         const rgToCheck = ripgrepConfig ?? config?.ripgrep ?? { command: 'rg' };
806:         if (whichSync(rgToCheck.command) === null) {
807:             errors.push(`ripgrep (${rgToCheck.command}) not found`);
808:         }
809:         const linuxDeps = checkLinuxDependencies({
810:             seccompConfig: config?.seccomp,
811:             bwrapPath: config?.bwrapPath,
812:             socatPath: config?.socatPath,
813:         });
814:         errors.push(...linuxDeps.errors);
815:         warnings.push(...linuxDeps.warnings);
816:     }
817:     else if (platform === 'windows') {
818:         let srtWin;
819:         try {
820:             srtWin = resolveSrtWin(config?.windows?.srtWin);
821:         }
822:         catch (e) {
823:             errors.push(e.message);
824:             return { done: { errors, warnings } };
825:         }
826:         return {
827:             windows: {
828:                 sublayerGuid: config?.windows?.sublayerGuid ?? config?.windows?.wfpSublayerGuid,
829:                 srtWin,
830:             },
831:         };
832:     }
833:     return { done: { errors, warnings } };
834: }
835: /**
836:  * Check sandbox dependencies for the current platform
837:  * @param ripgrepConfig - Ripgrep command to check. If not provided, uses config from initialization or defaults to 'rg'
838:  * @returns { warnings, errors } - errors mean sandbox cannot run, warnings mean degraded functionality
839:  */
840: function checkDependencies(ripgrepConfig) {
841:     const common = checkDependenciesCommon(ripgrepConfig);
842:     if ('done' in common)
843:         return common.done;
844:     return checkWindowsDependencies(common.windows);
845: }
846: /**
847:  * Async variant of {@link checkDependencies} — same result for the
848:  * same underlying state. On Windows the srt-win probes run via
849:  * `spawn` (never blocking the event loop) and concurrently; on other
850:  * platforms the checks are native and this simply wraps the sync
851:  * result. Windows callers should prefer this variant.
852:  */
853: async function checkDependenciesAsync(ripgrepConfig) {
854:     // Linux: resolve apply-seccomp first so its global-npm fallback
855:     // (`npm root -g`) runs off the event loop; the sync check below then
856:     // hits the shared path cache.
857:     if (getPlatform() === 'linux' && !config?.seccomp?.argv0) {
858:         await getApplySeccompBinaryPathAsync(config?.seccomp?.applyPath);
859:     }
860:     const common = checkDependenciesCommon(ripgrepConfig);
861:     if ('done' in common)
862:         return common.done;
