863:     return checkWindowsDependenciesAsync(common.windows);
864: }
865: /**
866:  * Build the read-deny / env-unset / env-set maps implied by the
867:  * `credentials` config.
868:  *
869:  * Only explicitly declared sources are restricted: `mode: 'deny'` file
870:  * entries join the read-deny set, `mode: 'deny'` env vars are unset, and
871:  * `mode: 'mask'` env vars are set to a fake value (whole-value sentinel,
872:  * the real value with extract-captured spans swapped for sentinels, or a
873:  * JWT-shaped fake for `decode: 'jwt'` / `maskClaims` entries) registered
874:  * in {@link sentinelRegistry} — see {@link buildMaskedEnvVars}.
875:  */
876: function getCredentialRestrictions(credentials, allowedDomains) {
877:     if (!credentials) {
878:         return {
879:             denyReadPaths: [],
880:             unsetEnvVars: [],
881:             setEnvVars: {},
882:             maskedFileBinds: [],
883:             maskedFileStoreDir: undefined,
884:             degradeToDenyPaths: [],
885:         };
886:     }
887:     const denyReadPaths = getCredentialDenyReadPaths(credentials);
888:     // Default injectHosts (= allowedDomains) is host-scoped: drop any
889:     // `:port` suffixes, otherwise the sentinel would carry an entry no bare
890:     // destination host can ever match and the credential would never inject.
891:     const defaultInjectHosts = [
892:         ...new Set((allowedDomains ?? []).map(stripDomainPatternPort)),
893:     ];
894:     const unsetEnvVars = [];
895:     for (const v of credentials.envVars ?? []) {
896:         if (v.mode === 'deny')
897:             unsetEnvVars.push(v.name);
898:     }
899:     // Masked env vars: read the real value from the host environment,
900:     // register sentinel(s), and set the variable to the fake value inside
901:     // the sandbox. degradeToUnsetNames carries variables whose extract
902:     // pattern matched nothing with onExtractNoMatch: "deny" — merged into
903:     // unsetEnvVars below so the value is withheld rather than exposed.
904:     const { setEnvVars, degradeToUnsetNames } = buildMaskedEnvVars(credentials.envVars ?? [], defaultInjectHosts, sentinelRegistry);
905:     unsetEnvVars.push(...degradeToUnsetNames);
906:     // Link masked AWS credentials into pairs so the proxy can re-sign
907:     // SigV4 requests (the signature is derived from the secret; header
908:     // substitution alone cannot fix it).
909:     registerAwsPairs(credentials.envVars ?? [], credentials.awsPairs, defaultInjectHosts, setEnvVars, awsPairRegistry);
910:     // Masked files: read the real bytes on the host, register a sentinel,
911:     // write it to a fake file in the manager-owned temp dir. Missing/unreadable
912:     // entries are skipped (same posture as an unset masked env var).
913:     // degradeToDenyPaths carries paths whose extract pattern matched
914:     // nothing with onExtractNoMatch: "deny" — merged into denyReadPaths
915:     // below so both the read-deny config and the platform builders see
916:     // them, and carried separately so they stay literal on the way there.
917:     const files = credentials.files ?? [];
918:     const { binds: maskedFileBinds, degradeToDenyPaths } = buildMaskedFileBinds(files, defaultInjectHosts, sentinelRegistry, maskedFileStore);
919:     return {
920:         denyReadPaths: [...new Set([...denyReadPaths, ...degradeToDenyPaths])],
921:         unsetEnvVars: [...new Set(unsetEnvVars)],
922:         setEnvVars,
923:         maskedFileBinds,
924:         maskedFileStoreDir: maskedFileStore.dirPath,
925:         degradeToDenyPaths,
926:     };
927: }
928: /**
929:  * Pure (side-effect-free) chokepoint for credential file-deny
930:  * paths — `credentials.files` entries with `mode: 'deny'`. Any
931:  * code that needs the credential→denyRead contribution routes
932:  * through here so a comparison predicate can read it without
933:  * touching {@link sentinelRegistry}.
934:  */
935: function getCredentialDenyReadPaths(credentials) {
936:     const files = credentials?.files ?? [];
937:     return [...new Set(files.filter(f => f.mode === 'deny').map(f => f.path))];
938: }
939: /**
940:  * The default write paths under a filesystem policy's read rules, for
941:  * getFsWriteConfig() and wrapWithSandbox() alike. Fed the entries as
942:  * configured, through the pure {@link getCredentialDenyReadPaths}: no glob
943:  * expansion and no credential masking, because getFsWriteConfig() is a
944:  * getter callers reach from permission checks and render paths. A mask entry
945:  * that degrades to a deny is a file and cannot cover a directory, so
946:  * leaving those out changes nothing.
947:  */
948: function defaultWritePathsUnder({ denyRead, allowRead, credentials, }) {
949:     return getDefaultWritePaths({
950:         denyRead: [...denyRead, ...getCredentialDenyReadPaths(credentials)],
951:         allowRead,
952:     });
953: }
954: /**
955:  * Union the explicit `filesystem.denyRead` with credential-derived
956:  * deny paths. The single source of "what files does this config
957:  * want read-denied" — all platforms route through here so a new
958:  * credential kind that contributes deny paths reaches every
959:  * backend.
960:  */
961: function unionDenyReadPaths(denyRead, credentialRestrictions) {
962:     return [...new Set([...denyRead, ...credentialRestrictions.denyReadPaths])];
963: }
964: /**
965:  * Strip a trailing `/**` from each read-path entry and, on Linux, replace
966:  * any remaining glob with what `expandGlob` returns for it (bubblewrap takes
967:  * concrete paths only). Other platforms match globs natively.
968:  *
969:  * `literalPaths` are the ones the library resolved itself (a masked
970:  * credential file that degraded to deny) — each names one file on disk, so
971:  * it is passed through whatever characters it contains. Expanded as a
972:  * pattern, a name holding `[` matches nothing and the deny is lost.
973:  */
974: function resolveReadPathEntries(paths, expandGlob, literalPaths = []) {
975:     const literal = new Set(literalPaths);
976:     return paths.flatMap(p => {
977:         const stripped = removeTrailingGlobSuffix(p);
978:         return getPlatform() === 'linux' &&
979:             !literal.has(p) &&
980:             containsGlobChars(stripped)
981:             ? expandGlob(p)
982:             : [stripped];
983:     });
984: }
985: /**
986:  * Strip a trailing `/**` and drop what is still a glob on Linux: bwrap needs
987:  * real paths. macOS subpath matching is recursive, so the strip is harmless
988:  * there and the filter never fires.
989:  */
990: function stripWriteGlobs(paths) {
991:     return paths
992:         .map(p => removeTrailingGlobSuffix(p))
993:         .filter(p => {
994:         if (getPlatform() === 'linux' && containsGlobChars(p)) {
995:             logForDebugging(`[Sandbox] Skipping glob write pattern on Linux: ${p}`);
996:             return false;
997:         }
998:         return true;
999:     });
1000: }
1001: function expandAllowReadGlob(pattern) {
1002:     const expanded = expandGlobPattern(pattern);
1003:     logForDebugging(`[Sandbox] Expanded allowRead glob pattern "${pattern}" to ${expanded.length} paths on Linux`);
1004:     return expanded;
1005: }
1006: /**
1007:  * The read policy of the initialized config, for inspection and display.
1008:  * On Linux, denyRead globs are collapsed to covering directory mounts against
1009:  * this config's allowRead and {@link getFsWriteConfig}'s allowOnly, so
1010:  * `denyOnly` is only sound alongside that write config and must not be handed
1011:  * to wrapCommandWithSandboxLinux with a different one.
1012:  */
1013: function getFsReadConfig() {
1014:     if (!config || config.filesystem.disabled) {
1015:         return { denyOnly: [], allowWithinDeny: [] };
1016:     }
1017:     // Credential deny paths are unioned with the caller's denyRead — never
1018:     // replacing it — so explicit filesystem restrictions always survive.
1019:     const credentialRestrictions = getCredentialRestrictions(config.credentials, config.network.allowedDomains);
1020:     // allowRead (re-allow within denied regions) is resolved first: the
1021:     // denyRead glob expansion collapses against it.
1022:     const allowPaths = resolveReadPathEntries(config.filesystem.allowRead ?? [], expandAllowReadGlob);
1023:     const reExposedPaths = [...allowPaths, ...getFsWriteConfig().allowOnly];
1024:     const unlistableDenyDirs = new Set();
1025:     const denyPaths = resolveReadPathEntries(unionDenyReadPaths(config.filesystem.denyRead, credentialRestrictions), pattern => expandReadDenyGlobLinux(pattern, reExposedPaths, unlistableDenyDirs), credentialRestrictions.degradeToDenyPaths);
1026:     return {
1027:         denyOnly: denyPaths,
1028:         allowWithinDeny: allowPaths,
1029:         unlistableDenyDirs: [...unlistableDenyDirs],
1030:     };
1031: }
1032: function getFsWriteConfig() {
1033:     if (!config) {
1034:         return { allowOnly: getDefaultWritePaths(), denyWithinAllow: [] };
1035:     }
1036:     if (config.filesystem.disabled) {
1037:         return { allowOnly: ['/'], denyWithinAllow: [] };
1038:     }
1039:     const allowPaths = stripWriteGlobs(config.filesystem.allowWrite);
1040:     const denyPaths = stripWriteGlobs(config.filesystem.denyWrite);
1041:     const allowOnly = [
1042:         ...defaultWritePathsUnder({
1043:             denyRead: config.filesystem.denyRead,
1044:             allowRead: config.filesystem.allowRead,
1045:             credentials: config.credentials,
1046:         }),
1047:         ...allowPaths,
1048:     ];
1049:     return {
1050:         allowOnly,
1051:         denyWithinAllow: denyPaths,
1052:     };
1053: }
1054: /**
1055:  * Build the Windows file-access set (deny stamps + sandbox-user
1056:  * grants) from `runtimeConfig`. Globs are expanded to concrete
1057:  * paths (point-in-time — a path appearing after this returns is NOT
1058:  * covered). Directory targets are accepted (the `(OI)(CI)` ACEs
1059:  * cover the subtree).
1060:  *
1061:  * The sandbox user has no inherent rights on real-user-owned files,
1062:  * so `allowWrite` (the working-tree roots) becomes a per-session
1063:  * `MODIFY_NO_FDC` ALLOW ACE for `<sb-SID>`, `allowRead` a
1064:  * `READ|EXECUTE` ALLOW ACE, and `denyRead`/`denyWrite` become an
1065:  * explicit DENY ACE for `<sb-SID>` on the target plus a
1066:  * `(OI)(CI) FILE_DELETE_CHILD` DENY on its parent.
1067:  */
1068: function computeWindowsFsAccessSet(c) {
1069:     const fs = c.filesystem;
1070:     // filesystem.disabled bypasses ALL filesystem rule generation —
1071:     // same as the macOS/Linux wrapWithSandbox path (readConfig /
1072:     // writeConfig left undefined). On Windows this means no ACL
1073:     // stamp/grant; credential FILE denies are dropped along with the
1074:     // rest (credential ENV: mode:'deny' is structural under the
1075:     // fresh srt-sandbox env; mode:'mask' sentinels are passed via
1076:     // the --env overlay).
1077:     if (fs?.disabled) {
1078:         return { grantRead: [], grantWrite: [], denyRead: [], denyWrite: [] };
1079:     }
1080:     const expand = expandWindowsFsPaths;
1081:     // `mode: 'deny'` — non-existent literals reach srt-win, which
1082:     // creates a placeholder chain and stamps it (deny lands on the
1083:     // exact target path). `mode: 'grant'` drops them (a grant on
1084:     // nothing is meaningless).
1085:     const denyRead = expand([
1086:         ...new Set([
1087:             ...(fs?.denyRead ?? []),
1088:             ...getCredentialDenyReadPaths(c.credentials),
1089:         ]),
1090:     ], { mode: 'deny' });
1091:     const denyWrite = expand(fs?.denyWrite ?? [], { mode: 'deny' });
1092:     return {
1093:         // `allowRead` also serves as `allowWithinDeny`: a file under a
1094:         // denied dir gets an explicit ALLOW ACE for the sandbox user,
1095:         // and explicit DENY on the parent doesn't override it because
1096:         // the recompose chokepoint orders deny-before-allow per-path.
1097:         grantRead: expand(fs?.allowRead ?? [], { mode: 'grant' }),
1098:         grantWrite: expand(fs?.allowWrite ?? [], { mode: 'grant' }),
1099:         denyRead,
1100:         denyWrite,
1101:     };
1102: }
1103: /**
1104:  * Snapshot the raw config fields that feed
1105:  * {@link computeWindowsFsAccessSet}. Used by updateConfig() to
1106:  * short-circuit the resolved-set diff (which re-runs glob
1107:  * expansion) when nothing relevant changed.
1108:  */
1109: function rawWindowsFsInputs(c) {
1110:     // Keyed exactly on what {@link computeWindowsFsAccessSet} reads.
1111:     // `network.allowedDomains` does NOT feed file-deny (only mask
1112:     // injectHosts), so a network-only updateConfig hits the cache.
1113:     return {
1114:         disabled: c.filesystem.disabled ?? false,
1115:         denyRead: [...c.filesystem.denyRead],
1116:         denyWrite: [...c.filesystem.denyWrite],
1117:         allowRead: [...(c.filesystem.allowRead ?? [])],
1118:         allowWrite: [...c.filesystem.allowWrite],
1119:         credFiles: getCredentialDenyReadPaths(c.credentials),
1120:     };
1121: }
1122: function setEq(a, b) {
1123:     if (a.length !== b.length)
1124:         return false;
1125:     const s = new Set(a);
1126:     return b.every(x => s.has(x));
1127: }
1128: function sameRawWindowsFsInputs(a, b) {
1129:     return (a.disabled === b.disabled &&
1130:         setEq(a.denyRead, b.denyRead) &&
1131:         setEq(a.denyWrite, b.denyWrite) &&
1132:         setEq(a.allowRead, b.allowRead) &&
1133:         setEq(a.allowWrite, b.allowWrite) &&
1134:         setEq(a.credFiles, b.credFiles));
1135: }
1136: /**
1137:  * True when `newConfig`'s file-deny inputs match what was
1138:  * stamped at initialize(). Compares raw inputs only (cheap,
1139:  * order-insensitive); never re-expands globs — updateConfig is
1140:  * warn-only on Windows and the resolved set wouldn't be used.
1141:  */
1142: function sameWindowsStampSet(newConfig) {
1143:     return (windowsFsRawInputs !== undefined &&
1144:         sameRawWindowsFsInputs(windowsFsRawInputs, rawWindowsFsInputs(newConfig)));
1145: }
1146: function getNetworkRestrictionConfig() {
1147:     if (!config) {
1148:         return {};
1149:     }
1150:     // Preserve an explicitly-empty allowlist: consumers need to distinguish
1151:     // "no network restriction configured" (absent) from "allowlist configured
1152:     // with zero entries" (block-all / ask-only). Stripping the empty array
1153:     // made a host app's restriction-status UI report an airgapped config as
1154:     // unrestricted. deniedHosts keeps the strip — an empty denylist and an
1155:     // absent one are semantically identical.
1156:     const allowedHosts = config.network.allowedDomains;
1157:     const deniedHosts = config.network.deniedDomains;
1158:     return {
1159:         allowedHosts,
1160:         ...(deniedHosts.length > 0 && { deniedHosts }),
1161:     };
1162: }
1163: function getAllowUnixSockets() {
1164:     return config?.network?.allowUnixSockets;
1165: }
1166: function getAllowAllUnixSockets() {
1167:     return config?.network?.allowAllUnixSockets;
1168: }
1169: function getAllowLocalBinding() {
1170:     return config?.network?.allowLocalBinding;
1171: }
1172: function getAllowMachLookup() {
1173:     return config?.network?.allowMachLookup;
1174: }
1175: function getIgnoreViolations() {
1176:     return config?.ignoreViolations;
1177: }
1178: function getEnableWeakerNestedSandbox() {
1179:     return config?.enableWeakerNestedSandbox;
1180: }
1181: function getEnableWeakerNetworkIsolation() {
1182:     return config?.enableWeakerNetworkIsolation;
1183: }
1184: function getAllowAppleEvents() {
1185:     return config?.allowAppleEvents;
1186: }
1187: function getRipgrepConfig() {
1188:     return config?.ripgrep ?? { command: 'rg' };
1189: }
1190: function getMandatoryDenySearchDepth() {
1191:     return config?.mandatoryDenySearchDepth ?? 3;
1192: }
1193: function getAllowGitConfig() {
1194:     return config?.filesystem?.allowGitConfig ?? false;
1195: }
1196: /**
1197:  * Union of session-level and per-call `git.safeDirectories`. Marks
1198:  * paths as `safe.directory` (dubious-ownership bypass) WITHOUT
1199:  * touching the write grant — the repo top-level for a subdirectory
1200:  * launch must NOT go in `filesystem.allowWrite`.
1201:  */
1202: function getGitSafeDirectories(customConfig) {
1203:     return [
1204:         ...(config?.git?.safeDirectories ?? []),
1205:         ...(customConfig?.git?.safeDirectories ?? []),
1206:     ];
1207: }
1208: function getSeccompConfig() {
1209:     return config?.seccomp;
1210: }
1211: function getProxyAuthToken() {
1212:     return proxyAuthToken;
1213: }
1214: function getProxyPort() {
1215:     return managerContext?.httpProxyPort;
1216: }
1217: function getSocksProxyPort() {
1218:     return managerContext?.socksProxyPort;
1219: }
1220: function getLinuxHttpSocketPath() {
1221:     return managerContext?.linuxBridge?.httpSocketPath;
1222: }
1223: function getLinuxSocksSocketPath() {
1224:     return managerContext?.linuxBridge?.socksSocketPath;
1225: }
1226: /**
1227:  * Wait for network initialization to complete if already in progress
1228:  * Returns true if initialized successfully, false otherwise
1229:  */
1230: async function waitForNetworkInitialization() {
1231:     if (!config) {
1232:         return false;
1233:     }
1234:     if (initializationPromise) {
1235:         try {
1236:             await initializationPromise;
1237:             return true;
1238:         }
1239:         catch {
1240:             return false;
1241:         }
1242:     }
1243:     return managerContext !== undefined;
1244: }
1245: async function wrapWithSandbox(command, binShell, customConfig, abortSignal, options) {
1246:     const platform = getPlatform();
1247:     const commandId = options?.commandId;
1248:     registerCommandText(command, options);
1249:     // filesystem.disabled bypasses ALL filesystem rule generation. Both
1250:     // platform wrappers treat readConfig/writeConfig === undefined as "no
1251:     // filesystem restrictions" (seatbelt emits `(allow file-write*)`; bwrap
1252:     // skips the `--ro-bind / /` root and all path binds).
1253:     //
1254:     // Precedence: when a caller passes a per-call filesystem override at all,
1255:     // its `disabled` (defaulting to false) wins outright. A global
1256:     // disabled=true must not silently discard a per-call tightening that
1257:     // omits the new key.
1258:     const fsDisabled = customConfig?.filesystem !== undefined
1259:         ? (customConfig.filesystem.disabled ?? false)
1260:         : (config?.filesystem.disabled ?? false);
1261:     // Credential env handling is independent of filesystem policy: unsetEnvVars /
1262:     // setEnvVars must be applied even when fsDisabled (the credential file
1263:     // deny-reads are dropped, but env scrubbing still happens).
1264:     const credentialRestrictions = getCredentialRestrictions(customConfig?.credentials ?? config?.credentials, customConfig?.network?.allowedDomains ?? config?.network?.allowedDomains);
1265:     // Get configs - use custom if provided, otherwise fall back to main config
1266:     // If neither exists, defaults to empty arrays (most restrictive)
1267:     // Always include default system write paths (like /dev/null, /tmp/claude)
1268:     let writeConfig;
1269:     let readConfig;
1270:     if (!fsDisabled) {
1271:         const userAllowWrite = stripWriteGlobs(customConfig?.filesystem?.allowWrite ??
1272:             config?.filesystem.allowWrite ??
1273:             []);
1274:         writeConfig = {
1275:             allowOnly: [
1276:                 ...defaultWritePathsUnder({
1277:                     denyRead: customConfig?.filesystem?.denyRead ??
1278:                         config?.filesystem.denyRead ??
1279:                         [],
1280:                     allowRead: customConfig?.filesystem?.allowRead ?? config?.filesystem.allowRead,
1281:                     credentials: customConfig?.credentials ?? config?.credentials,
1282:                 }),
1283:                 ...userAllowWrite,
1284:             ],
1285:             denyWithinAllow: stripWriteGlobs(customConfig?.filesystem?.denyWrite ??
1286:                 config?.filesystem.denyWrite ??
1287:                 []),
1288:         };
1289:         // Credential deny paths are unioned with the caller's denyRead — never
1290:         // replacing it — so explicit filesystem restrictions always survive.
1291:         // allowRead is resolved first: on Linux a denyRead glob's expansion is
1292:         // collapsed against the paths that re-expose contents under a denied
1293:         // directory (allowRead + allowWrite), so both must be final here.
1294:         const expandedAllowRead = resolveReadPathEntries(customConfig?.filesystem?.allowRead ?? config?.filesystem.allowRead ?? [], expandAllowReadGlob);
1295:         // The TLS-termination CA cert and the trust bundle the env vars point at
1296:         // (NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS etc.) must be readable by the child, even if their
1297:         // paths fall under a user-configured denyRead.
1298:         if (mitmCA) {
1299:             expandedAllowRead.push(mitmCA.certPath, mitmCA.trustBundlePath);
1300:         }
1301:         // Likewise the JVM proxy agent jar JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS points at.
1302:         if (javaAgentJarPath) {
1303:             expandedAllowRead.push(javaAgentJarPath);
1304:         }
1305:         const reExposedPaths = [...expandedAllowRead, ...writeConfig.allowOnly];
1306:         const unlistableDenyDirs = new Set();
1307:         const expandedDenyRead = resolveReadPathEntries(unionDenyReadPaths(customConfig?.filesystem?.denyRead ?? config?.filesystem.denyRead ?? [], credentialRestrictions), pattern => expandReadDenyGlobLinux(pattern, reExposedPaths, unlistableDenyDirs), credentialRestrictions.degradeToDenyPaths);
1308:         readConfig = {
1309:             denyOnly: expandedDenyRead,
1310:             allowWithinDeny: expandedAllowRead,
1311:             unlistableDenyDirs: [...unlistableDenyDirs],
1312:         };
1313:     }
1314:     // Check if network config is specified - this determines if we need network restrictions
1315:     // Network restriction is needed when:
1316:     // 1. customConfig has network.allowedDomains defined (even if empty array = block all)
1317:     // 2. OR config has network.allowedDomains defined (even if empty array = block all)
1318:     // An empty allowedDomains array means "no domains allowed" = block all network access
1319:     const hasNetworkConfig = customConfig?.network?.allowedDomains !== undefined ||
1320:         config?.network?.allowedDomains !== undefined;
1321:     // Network RESTRICTION is needed whenever network config is specified
1322:     // This includes empty allowedDomains which means "block all network"
1323:     const needsNetworkRestriction = hasNetworkConfig;
1324:     // Network PROXY is needed whenever network config is specified
1325:     // Even with empty allowedDomains, we route through proxy so that:
1326:     // 1. updateConfig() can enable network access for already-running processes
1327:     // 2. The proxy blocks all requests when allowlist is empty
1328:     const needsNetworkProxy = hasNetworkConfig;
1329:     // Wait for network initialization only if proxy is actually needed
1330:     if (needsNetworkProxy) {
1331:         await waitForNetworkInitialization();
1332:     }
1333:     // Check custom config to allow pseudo-terminal (can be applied dynamically)
1334:     const allowPty = customConfig?.allowPty ?? config?.allowPty;
1335:     const gitSafeDirectories = getGitSafeDirectories(customConfig);
1336:     switch (platform) {
1337:         case 'macos':
1338:             // macOS sandbox profile supports glob patterns directly, no ripgrep needed
1339:             return wrapCommandWithSandboxMacOS({
1340:                 command,
1341:                 commandId,
1342:                 needsNetworkRestriction,
1343:                 // Only pass proxy ports if proxy is running (when there are domains to filter)
1344:                 httpProxyPort: needsNetworkProxy ? getProxyPort() : undefined,
1345:                 socksProxyPort: needsNetworkProxy ? getSocksProxyPort() : undefined,
1346:                 proxyAuthToken: needsNetworkProxy ? proxyAuthToken : undefined,
1347:                 caCertPath: mitmCA?.trustBundlePath,
1348:                 javaAgentJarPath: needsNetworkProxy ? javaAgentJarPath : undefined,
1349:                 readConfig,
1350:                 writeConfig,
1351:                 unsetEnvVars: credentialRestrictions.unsetEnvVars,
1352:                 setEnvVars: credentialRestrictions.setEnvVars,
1353:                 maskedFileBinds: credentialRestrictions.maskedFileBinds,
1354:                 degradeToDenyPaths: credentialRestrictions.degradeToDenyPaths,
1355:                 allowUnixSockets: getAllowUnixSockets(),
1356:                 allowAllUnixSockets: getAllowAllUnixSockets(),
1357:                 allowLocalBinding: getAllowLocalBinding(),
1358:                 allowMachLookup: getAllowMachLookup(),
1359:                 ignoreViolations: getIgnoreViolations(),
1360:                 allowPty,
1361:                 allowGitConfig: getAllowGitConfig(),
1362:                 gitSafeDirectories,
1363:                 enableWeakerNetworkIsolation: getEnableWeakerNetworkIsolation(),
1364:                 allowAppleEvents: getAllowAppleEvents(),
1365:                 binShell,
1366:             });
1367:         case 'linux':
1368:             return wrapCommandWithSandboxLinux({
1369:                 command,
1370:                 commandId,
1371:                 needsNetworkRestriction,
1372:                 // Only pass socket paths if proxy is running (when there are domains to filter)
1373:                 httpSocketPath: needsNetworkProxy
1374:                     ? getLinuxHttpSocketPath()
1375:                     : undefined,
1376:                 socksSocketPath: needsNetworkProxy
1377:                     ? getLinuxSocksSocketPath()
1378:                     : undefined,
1379:                 httpProxyPort: needsNetworkProxy
1380:                     ? managerContext?.httpProxyPort
1381:                     : undefined,
1382:                 socksProxyPort: needsNetworkProxy
1383:                     ? managerContext?.socksProxyPort
1384:                     : undefined,
1385:                 proxyAuthToken: needsNetworkProxy ? proxyAuthToken : undefined,
1386:                 caCertPath: mitmCA?.trustBundlePath,
1387:                 javaAgentJarPath: needsNetworkProxy ? javaAgentJarPath : undefined,
1388:                 readConfig,
1389:                 writeConfig,
1390:                 unsetEnvVars: credentialRestrictions.unsetEnvVars,
1391:                 setEnvVars: credentialRestrictions.setEnvVars,
1392:                 maskedFileBinds: credentialRestrictions.maskedFileBinds,
1393:                 maskedFileStoreDir: credentialRestrictions.maskedFileStoreDir,
1394:                 enableWeakerNestedSandbox: getEnableWeakerNestedSandbox(),
1395:                 allowAllUnixSockets: getAllowAllUnixSockets(),
1396:                 binShell,
1397:                 ripgrepConfig: getRipgrepConfig(),
1398:                 mandatoryDenySearchDepth: getMandatoryDenySearchDepth(),
1399:                 allowGitConfig: getAllowGitConfig(),
1400:                 gitSafeDirectories,
1401:                 seccompConfig: getSeccompConfig(),
1402:                 bwrapPath: config?.bwrapPath,
1403:                 socatPath: config?.socatPath,
1404:                 observeSocketPath: linuxMonitor?.observeSocketPath,
1405:                 abortSignal,
1406:             });
1407:         case 'windows':
1408:             // Windows wraps to an argv array, not a shell string. Forcing
1409:             // callers through wrapWithSandboxArgv() means they spawn with
1410:             // {shell:false}, which is the security boundary that keeps the
1411:             // user's command bytes off the HOST shell.
1412:             throw new Error('wrapWithSandbox() returns a shell string and is not supported ' +
1413:                 'on Windows. Use SandboxManager.wrapWithSandboxArgv() and ' +
1414:                 'spawn the result with {shell: false}.');
1415:         default:
1416:             // Unsupported platform - this should not happen since isSandboxingEnabled() checks platform support
1417:             throw new Error(`Sandbox configuration is not supported on platform: ${platform}`);
1418:     }
1419: }
1420: /**
1421:  * Wrap `command` for the sandbox and return a spawn descriptor:
1422:  * `{ argv, env }`, suitable for
1423:  * `spawn(argv[0], argv.slice(1), {shell: false, env})`.
1424:  *
1425:  * On Windows this is the ONLY supported wrap method (see
1426:  * {@link wrapWithSandbox}); `env` is the broker process's spawn env
1427:  * — the sandboxed child gets a fresh `srt-sandbox` profile env with
1428:  * only the `--env` overlay baked into `argv` (see
1429:  * {@link wrapCommandWithSandboxWindows}). On
1430:  * macOS/Linux `argv` is `[binShell, '-c', <wrapWithSandbox result>]`
1431:  * (proxy env is baked into that command) and `env` is the unchanged
1432:  * `process.env`, so callers can spawn uniformly across platforms.
1433:  *
1434:  * @param cwd the working directory the caller will spawn the result
1435:  *   with. On Windows the child's cwd is whatever the caller passes
1436:  *   as the spawn `{cwd:}` option (there is no `--cwd` flag), and
1437:  *   the `safe.directory` git-config injection derives from this — so
1438:  *   pass the same value here as to `spawn({cwd})`. Defaults to
1439:  *   `process.cwd()`. Currently unused on macOS/Linux.
1440:  */
1441: async function wrapWithSandboxArgv(command, binShell, customConfig, abortSignal, cwd, options) {
1442:     const platform = getPlatform();
1443:     if (platform === 'windows') {
1444:         const hasNetworkConfig = customConfig?.network?.allowedDomains !== undefined ||
1445:             config?.network?.allowedDomains !== undefined;
1446:         if (hasNetworkConfig) {
1447:             await waitForNetworkInitialization();
1448:         }
1449:         const credentialRestrictions = getCredentialRestrictions(customConfig?.credentials ?? config?.credentials, customConfig?.network?.allowedDomains ?? config?.network?.allowedDomains);
1450:         // Per-exec FILE denies (customConfig only — the session-level
1451:         // config's denies were already stamped at initialize()).
1452:         // Paths go through `expandWindowsFsPaths` — the SAME
1453:         // chokepoint the session-level set uses (point-in-time glob
1454:         // expand, normalize, missing→drop) — so a per-exec entry
1455:         // resolves identically to its session-level equivalent.
1456:         // macOS/Linux per-exec already reuses session-level expansion;
1457:         // Windows now matches.
1458:         //
1459:         // The dedup against `windowsFsStampedSet` is an OPTIMIZATION,
1460:         // not a correctness gate: re-stamping a session-held path
1461:         // under the exec's distinct holder is refcount-safe but wastes
1462:         // a SetSecurityInfo round-trip.
1463:         //
1464:         // filesystem.disabled bypasses ALL filesystem rule generation
1465:         // — including credential-derived file denies — same ordering
1466:         // as session-level `computeWindowsFsAccessSet` (credential
1467:         // ENV: mode:'deny' is structural under the fresh srt-sandbox
1468:         // env; mode:'mask' sentinels are passed via the --env
1469:         // overlay).
1470:         // Per-exec allowRead/allowWrite throw — `srt-win exec` only
1471:         // exposes `--deny-*`; per-exec grants are not implemented.
1472:         const fsCfg = customConfig?.filesystem;
1473:         let perExecDenyRead = [];
1474:         let perExecDenyWrite = [];
1475:         if (!fsCfg?.disabled) {
1476:             if (fsCfg?.allowRead?.length || fsCfg?.allowWrite?.length) {
1477:                 throw new Error(`Per-exec filesystem.allowRead/allowWrite is not supported ` +
1478:                     `on Windows — \`srt-win exec\` only exposes per-exec ` +
1479:                     `denies. Set them at the session level (initialize()).`);
1480:             }
1481:             const rawRead = [
1482:                 ...(fsCfg?.denyRead ?? []),
1483:                 ...getCredentialDenyReadPaths(customConfig?.credentials),
1484:             ];
1485:             const rawWrite = fsCfg?.denyWrite ?? [];
1486:             // Skip on the dominant path (no per-exec fs or
1487:             // credential-file deny).
1488:             if (rawRead.length > 0 || rawWrite.length > 0) {
1489:                 const sessRead = new Set(windowsFsStampedSet?.denyRead ?? []);
1490:                 const sessWrite = new Set(windowsFsStampedSet?.denyWrite ?? []);
1491:                 const expand = expandWindowsFsPaths;
1492:                 perExecDenyRead = expand(rawRead, { mode: 'deny' }).filter(p => !sessRead.has(p));
1493:                 perExecDenyWrite = expand(rawWrite, { mode: 'deny' }).filter(p => !sessRead.has(p) && !sessWrite.has(p));
1494:             }
1495:         }
1496:         // Per-exec deny rides on argv (`acl stamp` reads stdin, but
1497:         // exec's stdin belongs to the child). The CreateProcessW
1498:         // length check lives in `wrapCommandWithSandboxWindows`
1499:         // where the full argv (incl. shell + user command) is known.
1500:         //
1501:         // The `denyReadPaths` half of the SESSION-level credentials
1502:         // is already unioned into the stamp set at initialize() time
1503:         // via `computeWindowsFsAccessSet`.
1504:         registerCommandText(command, options);
1505:         return wrapCommandWithSandboxWindows({
1506:             command,
1507:             commandId: options?.commandId,
1508:             httpProxyPort: hasNetworkConfig ? getProxyPort() : undefined,
1509:             socksProxyPort: hasNetworkConfig ? getSocksProxyPort() : undefined,
1510:             proxyAuthToken: hasNetworkConfig ? proxyAuthToken : undefined,
1511:             // mode:'deny' env vars are structurally absent (fresh
1512:             // srt-sandbox profile env). mode:'mask' sentinels are
1513:             // passed via the --env overlay so the sandboxed child sees
1514:             // the sentinel value, same as macOS/Linux.
1515:             setEnvVars: credentialRestrictions.setEnvVars,
1516:             denyRead: perExecDenyRead,
1517:             denyWrite: perExecDenyWrite,
1518:             // safe.directory: cwd + the resolved session-level write
1519:             // grants + explicit git.safeDirectories — the working-tree
1520:             // roots the sandbox user has MODIFY on plus any repo top-level
1521:             // the caller marks as safe without granting write.
1522:             cwd,
1523:             allowWrite: windowsFsStampedSet?.grantWrite,
1524:             gitSafeDirectories: getGitSafeDirectories(customConfig),
1525:             caCertPath: mitmCA?.trustBundlePath,
1526:             binShell: parseWindowsBinShell(binShell),
1527:             srtWin: customConfig?.windows?.srtWin
1528:                 ? resolveSrtWin(customConfig.windows.srtWin)
1529:                 : (srtWinSpawn ?? resolveSrtWin(config?.windows?.srtWin)),
1530:         });
1531:     }
1532:     // macOS/Linux: delegate to the existing string wrapper, then put
1533:     // the result behind `<shell> -c` so the caller's argv-spawn works.
1534:     if (typeof binShell === 'object') {
1535:         throw new Error('binShell object form is Windows-only; pass a shell path string ' +
1536:             'on macOS/Linux');
1537:     }
1538:     const wrapped = await wrapWithSandbox(command, binShell, customConfig, abortSignal, options);
1539:     const shell = binShell ?? '/bin/bash';
1540:     return { argv: [shell, '-c', wrapped], env: process.env };
1541: }
1542: /**
1543:  * Get the current sandbox configuration
1544:  * @returns The current configuration, or undefined if not initialized
1545:  */
1546: function getConfig() {
1547:     return config;
1548: }
1549: /**
1550:  * Update the sandbox configuration in place.
1551:  *
1552:  * **Network/allowlist changes are a live swap**: the running
1553:  * mux proxy reads `config.network.allowedDomains` /
1554:  * `deniedDomains` per-request (via `filterNetworkRequest`), so
1555:  * reassigning `config` here takes effect on the next connection
1556:  * with no proxy rebind and no port change — on every platform,
1557:  * including Windows. This is what lets a host enable/deny domains
1558:  * for already-running sandboxed children.
1559:  *
1560:  * Filesystem changes (denyRead/denyWrite) are NOT applied live:
1561:  * macOS bakes them into the seatbelt profile at wrap time, and
1562:  * Linux/Windows bake them into the bwrap argv / DENY-ACE set at
1563:  * wrap time. Call reset() + initialize() to apply a new
1564:  * filesystem config.
1565:  *
1566:  * @param newConfig - The new configuration to use
1567:  */
1568: function updateConfig(newConfig) {
1569:     if (getPlatform() === 'windows' &&
1570:         config &&
1571:         !sameWindowsStampSet(newConfig)) {
1572:         logForDebugging(`[Sandbox Windows] updateConfig: the resolved file-access set ` +
1573:             `(filesystem.* ∪ credentials.files) changed but the ACL ` +
1574:             `stamp/grant is session-wide — call reset() then initialize() ` +
1575:             `to apply. The previously-applied set stays in effect.`, { level: 'warn' });
1576:     }
1577:     // Built before anything is swapped, so a malformed range leaves the
1578:     // previous config fully in effect.
1579:     const nextGuard = createResolvedAddressGuard(newConfig.network);
1580:     // Deep clone the config to avoid mutations. structuredClone cannot clone
1581:     // functions, so pull filterRequest out, clone the rest, and put it back —
1582:     // a function reference is immutable in the sense that matters here.
1583:     const { filterRequest, ...rest } = newConfig.network;
1584:     config = structuredClone({ ...newConfig, network: rest });
1585:     config.network.filterRequest = filterRequest;
1586:     resolvedAddressGuard = nextGuard;
1587:     // Re-resolve parent proxy so hot-reload picks up changes. Note: the proxy
1588:     // servers capture `parentProxy` by value at creation, so changes here take
1589:     // effect only on re-initialize. This keeps the state consistent for the
1590:     // next initialize() call.
1591:     parentProxy = resolveParentProxy(newConfig.network.parentProxy);
1592:     logForDebugging('Sandbox configuration updated');
1593: }
1594: /**
1595:  * Lightweight cleanup to call after each sandboxed command completes.
1596:  *
1597:  * On Linux, bwrap creates empty files on the host filesystem as mount points
1598:  * when protecting non-existent deny paths (e.g. ~/.bashrc, ~/.gitconfig).
1599:  * These persist after bwrap exits. This function removes them.
1600:  *
1601:  * Safe to call on any platform — it's a no-op on macOS.
1602:  * Also called automatically by reset() and on process exit as safety nets.
1603:  */
1604: function cleanupAfterCommand() {
1605:     cleanupBwrapMountPoints();
1606: }
1607: /**
1608:  * How long to wait for a bridge process to exit after SIGTERM before
1609:  * escalating to SIGKILL.
1610:  *
1611:  * socat exits within ~10ms of SIGTERM; this is purely a safety margin.
1612:  * Keep it well below bun's default 5s test/hook timeout: when a bridge's
1613:  * `'exit'` event is missed entirely (a Linux-only Bun pidfd notification
1614:  * bug, oven-sh/bun#30301), this timer is the only thing that lets `reset()`
1615:  * make progress, and a 5000ms value here loses the race against the hook
1616:  * timer by a couple of milliseconds — that race was the dominant CI flake.
1617:  */
1618: const BRIDGE_EXIT_TIMEOUT_MS = 1500;
1619: /**
1620:  * SIGTERM a bridge process and resolve once it has exited.
1621:  *
1622:  * Returns immediately if the process has already exited (`.exitCode` /
1623:  * `.signalCode` set) — registering `.once('exit')` after the event has
1624:  * already been emitted produces a listener that never fires.
1625:  *
1626:  * Falls back to SIGKILL after {@link BRIDGE_EXIT_TIMEOUT_MS}.
1627:  */
1628: function killBridgeProcess(proc, label) {
1629:     // Already exited → 'exit' already emitted → a fresh once('exit') would
1630:     // never fire. Don't wait on it.
1631:     if (!proc.pid || proc.exitCode !== null || proc.signalCode !== null) {
1632:         return Promise.resolve();
1633:     }
1634:     try {
1635:         process.kill(proc.pid, 'SIGTERM');
1636:         logForDebugging(`Sent SIGTERM to ${label} bridge process`);
1637:     }
1638:     catch (err) {
1639:         if (err.code !== 'ESRCH') {
1640:             logForDebugging(`Error killing ${label} bridge: ${err}`, {
1641:                 level: 'error',
1642:             });
1643:         }
1644:         // ESRCH = process already gone; nothing to wait for either way.
1645:         return Promise.resolve();
1646:     }
1647:     return new Promise(resolve => {
1648:         let settled = false;
1649:         const done = () => {
1650:             if (settled)
1651:                 return;
1652:             settled = true;
1653:             clearTimeout(timer);
1654:             resolve();
1655:         };
1656:         proc.once('exit', () => {
1657:             logForDebugging(`${label} bridge process exited`);
1658:             done();
1659:         });
1660:         const timer = setTimeout(() => {
1661:             // Re-check liveness — the 'exit' may have raced us.
1662:             if (proc.exitCode === null && proc.signalCode === null) {
1663:                 logForDebugging(`${label} bridge did not exit, forcing SIGKILL`, {
1664:                     level: 'warn',
1665:                 });
1666:                 try {
1667:                     if (proc.pid)
1668:                         process.kill(proc.pid, 'SIGKILL');
1669:                 }
1670:                 catch {
1671:                     // Process may have already exited
1672:                 }
1673:             }
1674:             done();
1675:         }, BRIDGE_EXIT_TIMEOUT_MS);
1676:         // The bridge process is being torn down; this timer must not be the
1677:         // only thing keeping the event loop alive.
1678:         timer.unref?.();
1679:     });
1680: }
1681: /**
1682:  * Forcibly close an http.Server, including any in-flight requests.
1683:  *
1684:  * Plain `server.close()` waits for every active request to finish.
1685:  * The proxy may be mid-upstream-request when reset() runs (e.g. a test's
1686:  * curl was killed by --max-time while the proxy was still dialing the
1687:  * real example.com / api.github.com), and `dialDirect()` allows up to
1688:  * 30s before giving up. Combined with a socat fork that hasn't yet seen
1689:  * its unix-socket EOF, that leaves a fully-open inbound connection and
1690:  * `server.close()` never calls back. `closeAllConnections()` (Node 18.2+,
1691:  * also implemented in Bun) tears down those sockets so `close()` resolves
1692:  * immediately.
1693:  */
1694: function forceCloseHttpServer(server) {
1695:     return new Promise(resolve => {
1696:         // Must run *before* close(): in Bun, close() also detaches the
1697:         // underlying handle, so a closeAllConnections() called afterwards
1698:         // becomes a no-op and the close callback waits for the in-flight
1699:         // request to drain — defeating the purpose. With closeAllConnections()
1700:         // first, the connections are gone by the time close() runs and its
1701:         // callback fires immediately (Bun reports "Server is not running.",
1702:         // Node reports no error). Verified against both orderings.
1703:         if (typeof server.closeAllConnections === 'function') {
1704:             server.closeAllConnections();
1705:         }
1706:         server.close(error => {
1707:             if (error && error.message !== 'Server is not running.') {
1708:                 logForDebugging(`Error closing HTTP proxy server: ${error.message}`, {
1709:                     level: 'error',
1710:                 });
1711:             }
1712:             resolve();
1713:         });
1714:     });
1715: }
1716: async function reset() {
1717:     // Windows: release this session's sandbox-user ACEs. Best-effort
1718:     // — log anomalies rather than throw, so teardown always
1719:     // completes. Leftover ACEs are recoverable later via
1720:     // `srt-win acl recover` (which sweeps by trustee SID).
1721:     if (windowsFsStampedSet && windowsFsSbUserSid) {
1722:         const sb = windowsFsSbUserSid;
1723:         // Captured at initialize() — the SAME binary the grants/stamps
1724:         // were applied with, immune to `config` mutation between.
1725:         const srtWin = srtWinSpawn;
1726:         // 'restored'/'alreadyOriginal' are the pre- same-user-removal
1727:         // srt-win's success vocabulary; 'revoked'/'stillHeld' are the
1728:         // post-. Either is non-anomalous.
1729:         const ok = new Set(['revoked', 'stillHeld', 'restored', 'alreadyOriginal']);
1730:         const log = (kind, e) => {
1731:             if (!ok.has(e.status)) {
1732:                 logForDebugging(`[Sandbox Windows] ${kind}: '${e.path}' ${e.status} — ` +
1733:                     `ACE may be left in place; resolve and run ` +
1734:                     `\`srt-win acl recover\` to clear`, { level: 'warn' });
1735:             }
1736:         };
1737:         for (const e of revokeWindowsAcl({ sandboxUserSid: sb, srtWin }) ?? []) {
1738:             log('grant revoke', e);
1739:         }
1740:         for (const e of restoreWindowsAcl({ sandboxUserSid: sb, srtWin }) ?? []) {
1741:             log('deny restore', e);
1742:         }
1743:     }
1744:     windowsFsStampedSet = undefined;
1745:     windowsFsSbUserSid = undefined;
1746:     windowsFsRawInputs = undefined;
1747:     srtWinSpawn = undefined;
1748:     // windowsWfpVerified is NOT cleared — per-process, not per-session.
1749:     // Clean up any leftover bwrap mount points. Force past the
1750:     // active-sandbox counter — reset() means the session is over.
1751:     cleanupBwrapMountPoints({ force: true });
1752:     // Stop log monitor
1753:     if (logMonitorShutdown) {
1754:         logMonitorShutdown();
1755:         logMonitorShutdown = undefined;
1756:     }
1757:     if (linuxMonitor) {
1758:         linuxMonitor.stop();
1759:         linuxMonitor = undefined;
1760:     }
1761:     if (managerContext?.linuxBridge) {
1762:         const { httpSocketPath, socksSocketPath, httpBridgeProcess, socksBridgeProcess, } = managerContext.linuxBridge;
1763:         // Kill both bridges and wait for them to exit
1764:         await Promise.all([
1765:             killBridgeProcess(httpBridgeProcess, 'HTTP'),
1766:             killBridgeProcess(socksBridgeProcess, 'SOCKS'),
1767:         ]);
1768:         // Clean up sockets
1769:         if (httpSocketPath) {
1770:             try {
1771:                 fs.rmSync(httpSocketPath, { force: true });
1772:                 logForDebugging('Cleaned up HTTP socket');
1773:             }
1774:             catch (err) {
1775:                 logForDebugging(`HTTP socket cleanup error: ${err}`, {
1776:                     level: 'error',
1777:                 });
1778:             }
1779:         }
1780:         if (socksSocketPath) {
1781:             try {
1782:                 fs.rmSync(socksSocketPath, { force: true });
1783:                 logForDebugging('Cleaned up SOCKS socket');
1784:             }
1785:             catch (err) {
1786:                 logForDebugging(`SOCKS socket cleanup error: ${err}`, {
1787:                     level: 'error',
1788:                 });
1789:             }
1790:         }
1791:     }
1792:     // Close servers in parallel (only if they exist, i.e., were started by us)
1793:     const closePromises = [];
1794:     if (mitmCA) {
1795:         closePromises.push(disposeMitmCA(mitmCA));
1796:     }
1797:     if (muxProxyServer) {
1798:         closePromises.push(muxProxyServer.close().catch((error) => {
1799:             logForDebugging(`Error closing mux proxy server: ${error.message}`, {
1800:                 level: 'error',
1801:             });
1802:         }));
1803:     }
1804:     if (httpProxyServer) {
1805:         closePromises.push(forceCloseHttpServer(httpProxyServer));
1806:     }
1807:     if (socksProxyServer) {
1808:         const socksClose = socksProxyServer.close().catch((error) => {
1809:             logForDebugging(`Error closing SOCKS proxy server: ${error.message}`, {
1810:                 level: 'error',
1811:             });
1812:         });
1813:         closePromises.push(socksClose);
1814:     }
1815:     // Wait for all servers to close
1816:     await Promise.all(closePromises);
1817:     // Clear references
1818:     muxProxyServer = undefined;
1819:     httpProxyServer = undefined;
1820:     proxyAuthToken = undefined;
1821:     socksProxyServer = undefined;
1822:     managerContext = undefined;
1823:     initializationPromise = undefined;
1824:     parentProxy = undefined;
1825:     resolvedAddressGuard = createResolvedAddressGuard();
1826:     mitmCA = undefined;
1827:     javaAgentJarPath = undefined;
1828:     sentinelRegistry.clear();
1829:     awsPairRegistry.clear();
1830:     commandTextsByKey.clear();
1831:     maskedFileStore.dispose();
1832: }
1833: function getSandboxViolationStore() {
1834:     return sandboxViolationStore;
1835: }
1836: function annotateStderrWithSandboxFailures(command, stderr) {
1837:     if (!config) {
1838:         return stderr;
1839:     }
1840:     const violations = sandboxViolationStore.getViolationsForCommand(command);
1841:     if (violations.length === 0) {
1842:         return stderr;
1843:     }
1844:     let annotated = stderr;
1845:     annotated += EOL + '<sandbox_violations>' + EOL;
1846:     for (const violation of violations) {
1847:         annotated += violation.line + EOL;
1848:     }
1849:     annotated += '</sandbox_violations>';
1850:     return annotated;
1851: }
1852: /**
1853:  * Returns glob patterns from Edit/Read permission rules that are not
1854:  * fully supported on Linux. Returns empty array on macOS or when
1855:  * sandboxing is disabled.
1856:  *
1857:  * Patterns ending with /** are excluded since they work as subpaths.
1858:  */
1859: function getLinuxGlobPatternWarnings() {
1860:     // Only warn on Linux/WSL (bubblewrap doesn't support globs)
1861:     // macOS supports glob patterns via regex conversion
1862:     if (getPlatform() !== 'linux' || !config || config.filesystem.disabled) {
1863:         return [];
1864:     }
1865:     const globPatterns = [];
1866:     // Write paths take no globs at all on Linux: bubblewrap binds concrete
1867:     // paths, and nothing expands them.
1868:     const allPaths = [
1869:         ...config.filesystem.allowWrite,
1870:         ...config.filesystem.denyWrite,
1871:     ];
1872:     for (const path of allPaths) {
1873:         // Strip trailing /** since that's just a subpath (directory and everything under it)
1874:         const pathWithoutTrailingStar = removeTrailingGlobSuffix(path);
1875:         // Only warn if there are still glob characters after removing trailing /**
1876:         if (containsGlobChars(pathWithoutTrailingStar)) {
1877:             globPatterns.push(path);
1878:         }
1879:     }
1880:     // Read paths are expanded, so a glob there is supported — unless the
1881:     // pattern has no literal directory for the walk to start from (a wildcard
1882:     // in its first path component, `/**/*.pem`), which expands to nothing and
1883:     // leaves the entry unenforced.
1884:     for (const path of [
1885:         ...config.filesystem.denyRead,
1886:         ...(config.filesystem.allowRead ?? []),
1887:     ]) {
1888:         const baseDir = globPatternBaseDir(normalizePathForSandbox(path));
1889:         if (containsGlobChars(removeTrailingGlobSuffix(path)) &&
1890:             (baseDir === '' || baseDir === '/')) {
1891:             globPatterns.push(path);
1892:         }
1893:     }
1894:     return globPatterns;
1895: }
1896: // ============================================================================
1897: // Export as Namespace with Interface
1898: // ============================================================================
1899: /**
1900:  * Global sandbox manager that handles both network and filesystem restrictions
1901:  * for this session. This runs outside of the sandbox, on the host machine.
1902:  */
1903: export const SandboxManager = {
1904:     initialize,
1905:     isSupportedPlatform,
1906:     isSandboxingEnabled,

FILE dist/sandbox/mux-proxy.js
1: import { createServer, connect } from 'node:net';
2: import { join } from 'node:path';
3: import { tmpdir } from 'node:os';
4: import { unlink } from 'node:fs/promises';
5: import { logForDebugging } from '../utils/debug.js';
6: import { getPlatform } from '../utils/platform.js';
7: import { listenInRange } from './listen-in-range.js';
8: /**
9:  * First-byte values that select the SOCKS handler. SOCKS5's greeting is
10:  * `VER NMETHODS METHODS...` with VER=0x05; SOCKS4's CONNECT is
11:  * `VN CD DSTPORT...` with VN=0x04. Everything else on this port is HTTP:
12:  * request methods start with an ASCII uppercase letter (>= 0x41 'A'),
13:  * h2-prior-knowledge starts `PRI ` (0x50), and a stray TLS ClientHello
14:  * starts 0x16 — none of which collide with 0x04/0x05. A one-byte peek is
15:  * therefore an unambiguous discriminator.
16:  */
17: const SOCKS_FIRST_BYTES = new Set([0x04, 0x05]);
18: const DEFAULT_FIRST_BYTE_TIMEOUT_MS = 10000;
19: let backendSeq = 0;
20: function unixSocketPath() {
21:     // Keep it short — macOS sun_path is 104 bytes.
22:     return join(tmpdir(), `srt-mux-${process.pid}-${(backendSeq++).toString(36)}.sock`);
23: }
24: /**
25:  * Single-port proxy front-end that dispatches each connection to either the
26:  * SOCKS handler or the HTTP proxy based on the first byte the client sends.
27:  *
28:  * The HTTP leg cannot use `httpServer.emit('connection', socket)` because
29:  * Bun's `http.Server` does not implement that injection path (Node does).
30:  * Instead the HTTP backend listens on a private endpoint — a unix socket on
31:  * macOS/Linux, a localhost TCP port on Windows — and the mux pipes the
32:  * client socket to it. SOCKS connections are handed directly to the
33:  * library's per-connection entry, no extra hop.
34:  */
35: export function createMuxProxyServer(opts) {
36:     const firstByteTimeoutMs = opts.firstByteTimeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_FIRST_BYTE_TIMEOUT_MS;
37:     const isWindows = getPlatform() === 'windows';
38:     // Where the HTTP backend listens. Exactly one of these is set after
39:     // listenHttpBackend() resolves.
40:     let backendSocketPath;
41:     let backendTcpPort;
42:     // Track every accepted client socket so close() can tear them down
43:     // immediately rather than waiting for in-flight tunnels to drain.
44:     const openSockets = new Set();
45:     function dispatchHttp(client) {
46:         if (backendSocketPath === undefined && backendTcpPort === undefined) {
47:             // listenHttpBackend() must resolve before the front-end listens; this
48:             // guard is defense-in-depth in case a future caller reorders them.
49:             logForDebugging('mux: HTTP dispatch before backend bound; dropping', {
50:                 level: 'error',
51:             });
52:             client.destroy();
53:             return;
54:         }
55:         const upstream = backendSocketPath
56:             ? connect(backendSocketPath)
57:             : connect(backendTcpPort, '127.0.0.1');
58:         upstream.on('error', err => {
59:             // Surface a 502 with the errno code so callers (and CI logs) can tell
60:             // *why* the backend was unreachable instead of an opaque empty-reply.
61:             // Full error (including path) goes to debug logging only — the client
62:             // is our own sandboxed child, but there's no need to echo host paths.
63:             const code = err.code ?? 'ERR';
64:             logForDebugging(`mux: HTTP backend dial failed: ${err.message}`, { level: 'error' });
65:             if (!client.destroyed) {
66:                 client.end(`HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n` +
67:                     `mux backend dial failed (${code})\n`);
68:             }
69:         });
70:         client.on('error', () => upstream.destroy());
71:         client.once('close', () => upstream.destroy());
72:         upstream.once('close', () => client.destroy());
73:         client.pipe(upstream);
74:         upstream.pipe(client);
75:     }
76:     const server = createServer(client => {
77:         openSockets.add(client);
78:         client.once('close', () => openSockets.delete(client));
79:         client.on('error', err => logForDebugging(`mux: client socket error: ${err.message}`));
80:         const timer = setTimeout(() => {
81:             logForDebugging('mux: first-byte timeout; destroying connection');
82:             client.destroy();
83:         }, firstByteTimeoutMs);
84:         // Don't let a pending sniff keep the process alive.
85:         if (typeof timer.unref === 'function')
86:             timer.unref();
87:         client.once('readable', () => {
88:             clearTimeout(timer);
89:             const peek = client.read(1);
90:             if (!peek || peek.length === 0) {
91:                 // EOF before any byte — client connected and closed.
92:                 client.destroy();
93:                 return;
94:             }
95:             client.unshift(peek);
96:             if (SOCKS_FIRST_BYTES.has(peek[0])) {
97:                 opts.handleSocksConnection(client);
98:             }
99:             else {
100:                 dispatchHttp(client);
101:             }
102:         });
103:     });
104:     return {
105:         server,
106:         getPort() {
107:             const addr = server.address();
108:             return addr && typeof addr === 'object' ? addr.port : undefined;
109:         },
110:         async listenHttpBackend() {
111:             if (!isWindows) {
112:                 const path = unixSocketPath();
113:                 // A prior process with the same PID may have crashed without
114:                 // unlinking; clear any stale file so listen() doesn't EADDRINUSE.
115:                 await unlink(path).catch(() => { });
116:                 await new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
117:                     opts.httpServer.once('error', reject);
118:                     opts.httpServer.listen(path, () => {
119:                         opts.httpServer.removeListener('error', reject);
120:                         resolve();
121:                     });
122:                 });
123:                 backendSocketPath = path;
124:                 logForDebugging(`mux: HTTP backend listening on ${path}`);
125:                 return undefined;
126:             }
127:             // Windows: AF_UNIX support under Bun is unverified, so the backend
128:             // listens on a localhost TCP port inside the WFP-permitted range.
129:             // The mux→backend hop originates from the parent process (not the
130:             // sandboxed child), so WFP doesn't strictly require it; staying in
131:             // range just keeps the port surface predictable.
132:             await listenInRange(opts.httpServer, p => opts.httpServer.listen(p, '127.0.0.1'), opts.httpBackendPortRange, new Set());
133:             const addr = opts.httpServer.address();
134:             backendTcpPort = addr && typeof addr === 'object' ? addr.port : undefined;
135:             logForDebugging(`mux: HTTP backend listening on 127.0.0.1:${backendTcpPort}`);
136:             return backendTcpPort;
137:         },
138:         async close() {
139:             for (const s of openSockets)
140:                 s.destroy();
141:             openSockets.clear();
142:             await new Promise(resolve => server.close(() => resolve()));
143:             // The mux owns httpServer's listen lifecycle, so it owns close too.
144:             // sandbox-manager.reset() additionally calls forceCloseHttpServer()
145:             // for closeAllConnections() semantics; double-close is a no-op.
146:             await new Promise(resolve => opts.httpServer.close(() => resolve()));
147:             if (backendSocketPath) {
148:                 await unlink(backendSocketPath).catch(() => { });
149:                 backendSocketPath = undefined;
150:             }
151:             backendTcpPort = undefined;
152:         },
153:         unref() {
154:             server.unref();
155:             opts.httpServer.unref();
156:         },
157:     };
158: }
159: //# sourceMappingURL=mux-proxy.js.map

WORLD SETTINGS
package broker

// Row 140 M2 (design_docs/planned/w-workspace-exec-toolchain-effect.md §4.4):
// the srt settings World renders per episode × project at
// <state>/exec/<ep>.<project>.srt.json (0600). The shape is M0's measured one
// (design_docs/verification/world-row140-m0/m0_matrix.py): srt 0.0.78
// requires network.deniedDomains, and enableWeakerNetworkIsolation and
// allowAppleEvents are TOP-LEVEL keys. srt has no `summary` command, so
// World verifies the file itself: re-read, byte-compare with its canonical
// rendering, digest, and refuse a file it did not write.

import (
	"bytes"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"runtime"
)

// execSettingsSpec is everything one rendering depends on; every path is
// canonical (symlinks resolved) and absolute.
type execSettingsSpec struct {
	Worktree      string   // the episode worktree: writable, readable
	Cache         string   // <state>/exec-cache/<ep>/<project>: writable, readable
	OperatorHome  string   // denied for reading; anchors srt's two $HOME write defaults
	StateDir      string   // World's state dir: denied for reading
	WorkspaceRoot string   // every episode's parent: denied, so siblings are unreadable
	Protected     []string // canonical profile patterns
	ReadRoots     []string // the profile's read_roots plus each one's realpath
	SeccompDir    string   // linux only: the archived seccomp helper dir [M0, V43/V44]
	GOOS          string
}

type execSettingsFS struct {
	DenyRead   []string `json:"denyRead"`
	AllowRead  []string `json:"allowRead"`
	AllowWrite []string `json:"allowWrite"`
	DenyWrite  []string `json:"denyWrite"`
}

type execSettingsNet struct {
	AllowedDomains      []string `json:"allowedDomains"`
	DeniedDomains       []string `json:"deniedDomains"`
	AllowLocalBinding   bool     `json:"allowLocalBinding"`
	AllowAllUnixSockets bool     `json:"allowAllUnixSockets"`
}

type execSettings struct {
	Filesystem                   execSettingsFS  `json:"filesystem"`
	Network                      execSettingsNet `json:"network"`
	EnableWeakerNetworkIsolation bool            `json:"enableWeakerNetworkIsolation"`
	AllowAppleEvents             bool            `json:"allowAppleEvents"`
}

// execDenyNames are World's episode deny names (§4.4: the AILANG policy's
// names, plus `.git`, which srt's own list covers only in part, V5): each is
// denied as an absolute path under the worktree, a dir or a file alike.
//
// `.git/hooks` and `.git/config` come FIRST, before `.git` ([M2-linux], V50).
// When an episode's .git is a DIRECTORY, srt on Linux adds both to its own
// deny and stubs each absent one with a bind mount; a stub emitted after the
// read-only bind of .git makes bwrap abort ("Can't create file at
// …/.git/hooks: Read-only file system") and nothing runs. srt emits World's
// denies in order, before its own, so listed here the stubs are mounted while
// .git is still writable, and srt's later entries for them are duplicates.
// With a .git pointer file both are skipped (nothing can exist under a file).
func execDenyNames() []string {
	names := []string{".git/hooks", ".git/config", ".git"}
	names = append(names, episodeDenyDirs...)
	return append(names, episodeDenyFiles...)
}

// srtDefaultWritePaths are the paths srt always allows writing (V4); World
// denies each. /private/tmp/claude is darwin's alias of /tmp/claude.
func srtDefaultWritePaths(home, goos string) []string {
	paths := []string{"/tmp/claude"}
	if goos == "darwin" {
		paths = append(paths, "/private/tmp/claude")
	}
	return append(paths, filepath.Join(home, ".npm", "_logs"), filepath.Join(home, ".claude", "debug"))
}

func hostGOOS() string { return runtime.GOOS }

// renderExecSettings is the canonical rendering (§4.4): reads fenced by
// path list (D-140-1 = A), no network (D-140-2 = A), writes only to the
// worktree and the episode's exec cache, World's deny list and srt's four
// defaults closed.
func renderExecSettings(spec execSettingsSpec) ([]byte, error) {
	for _, p := range append([]string{spec.Worktree, spec.Cache, spec.OperatorHome, spec.StateDir, spec.WorkspaceRoot}, spec.ReadRoots...) {
		if !cleanAbs(p) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("broker: exec settings path %q is not clean and absolute", p)
		}
	}
	var denyWrite []string
	for _, n := range execDenyNames() {
		denyWrite = append(denyWrite, filepath.Join(spec.Worktree, n))
	}
	denyWrite = append(denyWrite, srtDefaultWritePaths(spec.OperatorHome, spec.GOOS)...)
	denyWrite = append(denyWrite, renderSrtProtected(spec.Protected, spec.Worktree, spec.GOOS)...)
	allowRead := dedupe(append([]string{spec.Worktree, spec.Cache}, spec.ReadRoots...))
	if spec.GOOS == "linux" {
		if !cleanAbs(spec.SeccompDir) {
			return nil, fmt.Errorf("broker: exec settings: linux needs the archived seccomp helper dir, got %q", spec.SeccompDir)
		}
		allowRead = append(allowRead, spec.SeccompDir)
	}
	s := execSettings{
		Filesystem: execSettingsFS{
			DenyRead:   []string{spec.OperatorHome, spec.StateDir, spec.WorkspaceRoot},
			AllowRead:  allowRead,
			AllowWrite: []string{spec.Worktree, spec.Cache},
			DenyWrite:  denyWrite,
		},
		Network: execSettingsNet{AllowedDomains: []string{}, DeniedDomains: []string{}},
	}
	data, err := json.MarshalIndent(s, "", " ")
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	return append(data, '\n'), nil
}

func dedupe(xs []string) []string {
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	out := make([]string, 0, len(xs))
	for _, x := range xs {
		if !seen[x] {
			seen[x] = true
			out = append(out, x)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// ExecSettingsError reports a settings file that is not the one World wrote:
// the call fails (recorded `failed`) and nothing runs under it.
type ExecSettingsError struct {
	Path string
	Why  string
}

func (e *ExecSettingsError) Error() string {
	return fmt.Sprintf("broker: exec settings %s is not World's rendering: %s", e.Path, e.Why)
}

// writeExecSettings writes data at path (0600, atomically), then verifies it
// and returns the settings_digest.
func writeExecSettings(path string, data []byte) (string, error) {
	if err := writeFileAtomic(path, data); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("broker: write exec settings: %w", err)
	}
	if err := verifyExecSettings(path, data); err != nil {
		return "", err
	}
	sum := sha256.Sum256(data)
	return "sha256:" + hex.EncodeToString(sum[:]), nil
}

// verifyExecSettings refuses anything but a regular 0600 file holding
// exactly World's canonical bytes.
func verifyExecSettings(path string, canonical []byte) error {
	info, err := os.Lstat(path)
	if err != nil {
		return &ExecSettingsError{Path: path, Why: err.Error()}
	}
	if !info.Mode().IsRegular() || info.Mode().Perm() != 0o600 {
		return &ExecSettingsError{Path: path, Why: fmt.Sprintf("mode %v, want a regular 0600 file", info.Mode())}
	}
	got, err := os.ReadFile(path)
	if err != nil {
		return &ExecSettingsError{Path: path, Why: err.Error()}
	}
	if !bytes.Equal(got, canonical) {
		return &ExecSettingsError{Path: path, Why: "its bytes differ from the canonical rendering"}
	}
	return nil
}

host/broker/exec_settings.go:45: 	AllowedDomains      []string `json:"allowedDomains"`
